Which MacBook to Buy (2026): Here’s Which Laptop Is Right for You

📅 08 Feb 2018 | ⏱️ 31 min read (6150 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~31 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • MacBooks went to some adventurous upcoming places this year.
  • Having tested every upcoming MacBook you can buy, I can guide you to the right laptop for your budget and performance needs.
  • For more recommendations, check out the rest of our computer buying guides, like Best Laptops, Best Mac Desktops, Best Cheap Laptops, Best iPads, and Best MacBook Accessories.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

MacBooks went to some adventurous upcoming places this year. The MacBook Neo pushes the boundaries of how cheap and low-powered a MacBook could go, while the OLED MacBook Pro takes it in the opposite direction. While the midyear price hike put a damper on all the new releases, prices won’t be going down anytime soon.

Having tested every upcoming MacBook you can buy, I can guide you to the right laptop for your budget and performance needs.

For more recommendations, check out the rest of our computer buying guides, like Best Laptops, Best Mac Desktops, Best Cheap Laptops, Best iPads, and Best MacBook Accessories.

Updated November 2026: I’ve added notes from my testing of the M6 MacBook Pro and OLED MacBook Pros, along with additional buying advice given the upcoming prices and rumors about future updates.

Although the MacBook Neo is more affordable, and the M5 MacBook Pro offers a better display with the far more powerful M5 Pro and Max chips, the MacBook Air remains the model I recommend for most people. The 2026 M5 refresh isn’t particularly exciting, but if your livelihood depends on sitting in front of a MacBook all day, it’s the best option.

Industry observers note that the starting price for the 13-inch model is now $1,299, up $200 from before. Notably, for much of last year, you could buy this laptop for as little as $750. That’s a painful reality, but it doesn’t change my recommendation that this is the MacBook model most people should buy.

In a recent development, although the exterior of the MacBook Air hasn’t changed since 2021, Apple has slowly evolved the laptop into something that feels airy and near-weightless. Most consumers need not worry about having too many tabs or applications open, eating up all that memory. You won’t be sitting around waiting for a file to download, because the SSD is blazing fast. With support for up to two 5K external monitors, the MacBook Air can function as a proper workstation when paired with a docking station. The 12-megapixel, 1080p webcam is plenty good for video calls.

Recent findings suggest that what matters most is that the M5 can do far more than most people will ever ask of their MacBook Air. Apple has boosted the GPU so much over the past generations that the M5 is actually on par with the M3 Pro. You’ll probably spend most of your day in browser tabs, Slack, Zoom, office applications, and spreadsheets, but the MacBook Air can just as easily handle Photoshop or Lightroom. You can even dabble in video editing or some light gaming if you want. If you were a professional video editor, you’d likely be bothered by the render times. But if it’s more of a hobby or side project, the M5 MacBook Air likely won’t impede your flow. Again, that’s where the MacBook Air really lives up to its do-it-all reputation.

As always, there are two sizes, measured diagonally: 13.6-inch and 15.3-inch. Aside from the $200 price gap, the screen size and speakers are the only notable differences between the two. Apple even scales up the pixel density to make sure the display on the 15-inch model looks just as sharp. The speakers on the 15-inch model sound incredible, second only to the 16-inch MacBook Pro. But choosing between the two sizes really comes down to how you use your laptop. If you have it plugged into an external monitor most days, you may as well get the 13-inch model and save yourself the extra space when you need to carry it around. But if a laptop is your primary machine, having that 15.3-inch screen really makes a difference, especially for more complicated applications or for using Split View.

It has been revealed that as you may notice, the M5 MacBook Air now starts with 512 GB of storage. That’s twice what previous models packed and helps to rationalize the price gap between the Neo and the Air. Having 512 GB of storage means you won’t have to worry about filling up your drive right away. This kind of headroom allows the technology to fade into the background—a design philosophy Apple has always championed. If you are a power user, consider adding more memory. Remember, MacBook memory and internal storage aren’t expandable down the road.

Read my in-depth comparison of the MacBook Neo and MacBook Air to see how they stack up.

After years of rumors, Apple has introduced a newly introduced MacBook Pro with never-before-seen features—most notably, the tandem PROLED XDR touchscreen. That’s right: this MacBook Pro is the first to ever have a touch-capable display, and you can now interact with it directly with your finger. Many people will be drawn in by the novelty of the feature (even though it’s been available on Windows laptops for almost a decade now), but I am skeptical about how useful it will be for day-to-day tasks. You will still primarily use the keyboard and trackpad, but I can see how the touchscreen would help in certain situations. Apple has made some optimizations to make the interface more touch-friendly, though I think there’s still room for improvement.

But don’t get me wrong: This MacBook Pro’s screen is the real deal. I’ve never seen a screen quite like this. Despite OLED’s reputation for not being bright enough, Apple’s is different. It delivers the insane contrast and clarity you’d expect from OLED, but with a maximum brightness that’s hundreds of nits higher than the previous-gen Mini-LED MacBook Pros.

It has a few tricks up its sleeve too, such as the return of the glow-up Apple logo on the lid and the hole-punch camera to replace the notch. As someone who has never gotten used to that ugly notch, that might be the change I was most thrilled to see. Apple even brought Dynamic Island from the iPhone to the MacBook Pro, using that hole creatively while hiding the camera. All in all, there’s a lot to be impressed by here.

Recent findings suggest that the only real concern is that it still uses the older M5 Pro or M5 Max chip. These are still some of Apple’s most powerful chips, but they have been out for over a year. This is the first time Apple isn’t introducing fresh chips alongside its new MacBook Pro in the past six years. Rumors indicate that the organization may be skipping the M6 Pro and M6 Max altogether. That’s made stranger by the fact that Apple is keeping the previous-gen models in the lineup—another uncommon move.

In a recent development, there’s a $400 difference between the 2025 M5 Pro and the 2025 PROLED M5 Pro, and for this pro-level demographic of buyers, it’s a relatively small price to pay for all the upgrades. I appreciate that Apple kept the older models around for those who want the extra performance without the fancy, more expensive display. On the other hand, if Apple wasn’t at the moment selling them, third-party retailers might have dropped the price more while they were still in stock.

Recent findings suggest that the MacBook Neo (7/10, WIRED Recommends) came out earlier this year, and it had a lot to prove. That’s especially true since it debuted at just $599, an unheard-of price point for Apple laptops—much less than any other model, even before recent price hikes took effect. And even though the MacBook Neo now starts at $699 after those price increases, it remains an aggressively affordable option. To keep pricing low, Apple had to make the following compromises:.

That’s a major list, and the memory limitation is the most significant drawback. Unlike on the MacBook Air, you can find the limits of the Neo fairly easily—and not on purpose. If you’re coming from a 16 GB MacBook Air, for example, you likely developed a habit of keeping idle applications or tabs open. On the MacBook Neo, you’ll need to be a bit more aware of what’s open to avoid slowdowns. You’ll also want to know which ports you’re using, since only the rear USB-C port supports an external display. The other USB-C port is only USB 2.0, rated at a max of 480 megabits per second. That’s definitely not the one you want to use for file transfers. If you don’t have the Touch ID model, you may even need to watch who you’re sitting next to in a coffee shop when entering passwords. We haven’t had to worry about these things on laptops for many years.

In exchange, Apple delivers an incredible front-of-screen experience on the MacBook Neo, never before seen on a laptop of this price. The display is sharper and brighter than anything else you can buy for $699, while the keyboard and trackpad are both excellent. Build quality is every bit as strong as any other Apple product, and at 0.50 inches thick, it’s still quite portable.

On top of all that, the Neo has three really good features over the Air. There’s a wider range of color options—and a lot of people will gravitate toward the Neo for that alone. My favorite change is the lack of a camera notch. While the bezels are slightly thicker, I’d still prefer a uniform screen without an ugly notch blocking part of my view. Perhaps most meaningfully, the Neo is reportedly the most repairable MacBook in the lineup, swapping out adhesives for screws on components such as the battery and speakers. This is great for classrooms and businesses hoping to keep fleets of these up to date without contributing as much to the mounting e-waste problem.

According to recent reports, for most of the time, you’ll enjoy using the MacBook Neo. As a parent, this should be the go-to device for high school and college students. It also works equally well as a secondary laptop away from your workstation or as a small travel laptop.

Industry observers note that the newer PROLED MacBook Pros are flashier, but they use the same M5 Pro or M5 Max chips as the previous-gen models. And interestingly, Apple still sells these older ones. So, while these 2025 models don’t have touchscreen OLED displays, they’re every bit as powerful. You aren’t missing out on any performance, and if the rumors hold, these will be the top-of-the-line MacBook Pro chips for a while.

Of course, these MacBook Pros are still very expensive, though. Like its PROLED sibling, the standard M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pro (8/10, WIRED Recommends) aren’t for the average person. The price alone should clue you in, but if you are the target audience and willing to pay well over $4,000 for a powerful laptop, the M5 Max MacBook Pro is unmatched in its capabilities. As always, the “Max” is primarily about considerably more GPU performance. Along with the option of two extra CPU cores, you can get up to 40 GPU cores, each with a built-in AI accelerator.

In a recent development, the M5 Max’s power applies to three use cases: creative applications, on-device AI processing, and gaming. Whether it’s 3D modeling, video editing, or some other resource-heavy application, the M5 Max MacBook Pro will tear through it. But AI performance also takes a significant leap. I tested a 17-billion-parameter Llama-2 model, which ran at conversational speed locally (the speed an AI model runs on a device), and it was 31 percent faster than running the same model on the M3 Max MacBook Pro.

Then there’s gaming. Nobody is going to buy the MacBook Pro for its gaming prowess alone, but it’s there when you want it. For the first time ever, you can hit over 60 frames per second in Cyberpunk 2077 on the Ultra preset with no upscaling. That’s an RTX 5070 Ti-level of laptop gaming performance. And unlike laptops that actually have that GPU, the MacBook Pro gets incredible battery life. Lastly, creative professionals will appreciate the faster storage speeds than previous generations.

The Mini-LED display is as gorgeous as ever, even if it pales in comparison to the fresh OLED models. You get a solid selection of ports, including three Thunderbolt 5 ports that offer ample external display support. It’s at the top of its class in nearly every aspect. Beyond CPU/GPU performance, you can choose between two screen sizes that perform similarly.

If this machine is overkill, you can drop down to the M5 Pro, which starts at $2,499 but is a power champ in its own right. Its multi-core and GPU performance are also stronger than the latest M6 (see below).

Recent findings suggest that the MacBook Pro is a slight misnomer because there are really three variants. I’ve talked about the PROLED and M5 Pro/M5 Max versions above. The third, the base model, is the latest M6 MacBook Pro, and despite using the latest chip, it’s the cheapest of the Pro options. Unfortunately, it’s also the hardest to recommend. That has less to do with the laptop itself and more to do with its price and how it fits into the lineup.

Like its M5 predecessor, it remains a beautiful, well-made laptop with all the high-end features you’d expect from a MacBook Pro. That includes the excellent speakers and very bright Mini-LED display. But it costs $1,999. Keep in mind that the M5 Pro MacBook Pro is $2,499, and you can still buy the M5 model for $1,799 or the 15-inch M5 MacBook Air for $1,499—hence the “awkward middle child” designation.

Industry observers note that to be fair, you get a terabyte of storage and 16 GB of RAM, while the M5 MacBook Pro started with 512 GB of storage. Apple also kept the starting price the same—that is, the price after Apple increased pricing across the board (the base MacBook Pro used to start at $1,699), but let’s not go there.

Sources indicate that the M6 chip is certainly faster than the M5, but it’s less of a massive leap forward than in previous generations. You’re looking at about a 15 percent improvement in CPU performance. I think the bigger disappointment is only a 9 percent improvement in graphics. That’s been an area where previous generational chip leaps have been more significant.

If you are considering the M6 MacBook Pro, I strongly suggest you look at the 15-inch M5 MacBook Air. It starts at a much lower price for the base configuration, but you can bump up the specs and still stay below $2,000. Yes, the MacBook Air is a different machine, but it has the performance that would impress many MacBook Pro users.

According to recent reports, all MacBooks were updated in 2026, making it a good time to buy one. The problem is that on June 25, Apple dramatically increased the price of all the MacBooks (and iPads) to varying degrees. Here’s a breakdown of the fresh starting prices, with increases ranging from $100 to $400:.

It’s rare for Apple to raise prices suddenly, especially when the change doesn’t coincide with a product refresh. What made this update especially unusual, though, is that only a few months had passed since the MacBook Neo introduced. Apple blamed the price spikes on memory and storage increases, stating that AI data centers had “created an extraordinary surge in demand” never seen before.

Sources indicate that so yes, the better time to buy a MacBook would have been earlier this year. While Apple notes that it is “working tirelessly to find solutions,” I wouldn’t expect these prices to come down anytime soon. Predictions around how long this memory shortage will last are measured in years, not months.

At the moment, only the 14-inch MacBook Pro gets the latest M6 chip. Rumors suggest Apple will skip the M6 Pro and M6 Max in this generation, saving the chip upgrade for the MacBook Pro until the M7 Pro and M7 Max.

A Breakdown of Each M-Series Chip.

In a recent development, apple’s processors are scattered across different MacBook models, and you can find older models online from third-party retailers, either latest or refurbished. If you do stumble upon older chips, you might be wondering how they compare to newer options. Here, get a breakdown of the differences to consider.

M6: Apple has already released its latest M6 line of chips, though the rollout has been slower than normal. As of this year, it’s only available in the base 14-inch MacBook Pro, iMac, and Mac Mini. I expect to see this arrive on devices like the iPad Pro and MacBook Air eventually, but the rumors about the rest of the M6 lineup are perplexing. Reports indicate Apple will skip the M6 Pro and M6 Max entirely and jump straight to the M7 Pro and M7 Max, perhaps in late 2027. That makes sense given what Apple just introduced with the OLED MacBook Pro, which uses the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as the previous generation.

M5: Apple launched the M5 chips in late 2025 with the 14-inch MacBook Pro, iPad Pro, and Vision Pro. The base M5 offers up to a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU, though a lower-tier 9-core CPU is still available on the iPad Pro. The M5 is about 10 to 15 percent faster in CPU performance than the M4 and takes a significant step up in GPU, AI workloads, and even storage speed. The M5 is now also available on the MacBook Air.

In a recent development, M5 Pro: These more powerful M5 chips are currently available in the 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros. The M5 Pro comes with a 15-core CPU and a 16-core GPU, with an option to upgrade to an 18-core CPU and a 20-core GPU. As with previous generations, the Pro chip gets all the same benefits as those in the M5 architecture but adds more cores and improved memory bandwidth. The biggest advantage is in GPU and on-device AI performance. This time around, however, both the M5 Pro and M5 Max also debuted the “Fusion Architecture,” a new version of UltraFusion (previously used only on the Ultra chips) that combines two dies across a superfast interconnect.

Sources indicate that M5 Max: The M5 Max is the M5 Pro—only with more GPU power. You can get up to 40 GPU cores, putting the MacBook Pro on par with high-end gaming laptops in graphics performance. With neural accelerators built into each GPU core, you’ve got one of the most powerful AI laptops on the market. It comes in either the MacBook Pro or the Mac Studio.

M5 Ultra: Like the other “Ultra” chips, the M5 Ultra is available only in the 2026 Mac Studio. It’s by far Apple’s most powerful chip, but you can’t configure it in a MacBook.

Industry observers note that M4: The M4 launched in 2024. It has a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU. Apple claims the M4 delivers 1.8 times faster CPU performance and 2.2 times faster GPU performance than the M1. Meanwhile, the neural engine is more than three times faster than the original and twice as fast as the M3. It also starts with 16 GB of unified memory, which helps to power Apple Intelligence (the company’s suite of artificial intelligence features) more smoothly. It’s available on the 14-inch MacBook Pro (2024), iMac (2024), and MacBook Air (13-inch and 15-inch, 2025).

Sources indicate that M4 Pro: The M4 Pro has a 14-core CPU (which Apple claims is up to 1.9 times faster than the M1 Pro) and up to a 20-core GPU, with up to 64 GB of unified memory. Built on a second-generation 3-nanometer process, it also supports enhanced GPU features like mesh shading and ray tracing—the latter of which is now twice as fast as on M3 chips. You’ll find it on the 2024 MacBook Pro (14-inch and 16-inch) and Mac Mini (2024).

In a recent development, M4 Max: This chip has a 16-core CPU and up to a 40-core GPU with support for up to 128 GB of unified memory. Apple indicates the CPU is up to 2.2 times faster than the M1 Max, while the GPU is up to 1.9 times faster. Like the M4 Pro, it supports mesh shading and ray tracing. The M4 Max is available as an option on the 2024 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro, and you can also get it as an option in the current Mac Studio.

M3: The M3 was available on the 14-inch MacBook Pro (late 2023), 13-inch MacBook Air (2024), 15-inch MacBook Air (2024), and 24-inch iMac (2023). It packs an 8-core CPU and up to a 10-core GPU, with up to 24 GB of unified memory. Compared with the M1, Apple claimed CPU performance was up to 35 percent faster and GPU performance up to 65 percent faster. The tech giant said the CPU and GPU are both 20 percent faster than the M2. As with the M1 and M2, it was great for basic tasks like word processing, sending emails, using spreadsheets, and light gaming. The 13-inch and 15-inch MacBook Air also supported two external displays (one up to 6K at 60 Hz and another up to 5K at 60 Hz).

M3 Pro: With a 12-core CPU and an 18-core GPU, Apple claimed the M3 Pro’s GPU was only up to 10 percent faster than the M2 Pro, making it a marginal upgrade from its predecessor. Compared with the M1 Pro, however, the M2 Pro was up to 40 percent faster in GPU performance and 20 percent faster in CPU performance. It was available on the 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro from 2023. It was the ideal in-between for those who needed a chip more powerful than the M3 but didn’t need the full power of the M3 Max.

M3 Max: The next step up from the M2 Max. It had a 16-core CPU, 40-core GPU, and up to 128 GB of unified memory. According to Apple, the CPU performance was up to 80 percent faster than the M1 Max and up to 50 percent faster than the M2 Max. As for GPU performance, it was said to be up to 50 percent faster than the M1 Max and 20 percent faster than the M2 Max. The M3 Max was available on the 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro (late 2023).

Industry observers note that M3 Ultra: Apple introduced the M3 lineup in 2023, but only revealed the M3 Ultra in 2025. It was even better than the latest M4 Max and M5 at the time. It had up to 32 CPU cores (24 performance cores) and up to 80 GPU cores. Apple claimed it was up to 2.5 times faster than the M1 Ultra. It also came with 96 GB of unified memory, upgradable to 512 GB, and up to 16 TB of SSD storage. This chip was available only on the 2025 Mac Studio.

Sources indicate that M2: The M2 was an entry-level chip like the M1, with slightly more processing power. It packed an 8-core CPU and up to a 10-core GPU (two more GPU cores than its predecessor), and supported up to 24 GB of unified memory. Apple said the second-generation chip has an 18 percent faster CPU and a GPU that’s 35 percent more powerful than its earlier version. The M2 was great for daily tasks like word processing and web browsing, but tasks such as editing multiple streams of 4K footage and 3D rendering should be reserved for Pro or Max chips. It was available in the MacBook Air (13-inch, 2022), MacBook Air (15-inch, 2022), and MacBook Pro (13-inch, 2022).

It has been revealed that M2 Pro: The M2 Pro had up to 12 cores in the CPU and up to a 19-core GPU, with up to 32 GB of unified memory. Apple claimed performance was up to 20 percent faster than with the 10-core M1 Pro and graphics were 30 percent faster. We recommended this chip for intermediate video and photo editors. It was a marginal upgrade compared with the M1 Pro, but it was the best option for those who wanted a more future-proof processor. You could find it in the MacBook Pro (14-inch and 16-inch) from early 2023 and the Mac Mini (2023).

M2 Max: The M2 Max packs up to a 12-core CPU and up to a 38-core GPU (with support for up to 96 GB of unified memory). According to Apple, graphics are 30 percent faster than on the M1 Max. The M2 Max is an excellent choice for those who work with graphics-intensive content, including graphic design, 3D modeling, and heavy-duty video footage. But as with the M2 Pro, it’s an incremental upgrade if you’re coming from an M1 Max. It’s available in the MacBook Pro (14-inch and 16-inch) released in early 2023 and the Mac Studio (2023).

M2 Ultra: The successor to the M1 Ultra, the M2 Ultra was available in the second-generation Mac Studio and the Mac Pro (2023). Composed of two M2 Max chips, using Apple’s UltraFusion technology, the M2 Ultra had a 24-core CPU and a GPU configurable with 60 or 76 cores. Apple claimed the CPU delivered up to 20 percent faster performance and that the GPU was up to 30 percent faster than the M1 Ultra. This was the chip to get if you were working with extremely heavy-duty content that you believed the M1 Ultra, M2 Pro, or M2 Max simply couldn’t handle. You’d have known if you needed a chip this robust.

M1: Introduced in 2020, the M1 was Apple's first custom silicon designed for the Mac. The M1 had an 8-core CPU and up to an 8-core GPU. Originally, you could get up to 16 GB of unified memory (RAM) for an extra cost, but now you can only purchase the 8-GB model. It was much faster than any previous Intel-powered MacBook Pro and the practical choice for most people. It packed more than enough processing power for day-to-day tasks and even light gaming. It could also handle more intense jobs, like photo editing. Long after its initial release, Apple continued to sell the M1 MacBook Air through Walmart for just $599, a killer price for this laptop. The MacBook Neo has since replaced it, using the A18 Pro chip from the iPhone 16 Pro models.

Industry observers note that M1 Pro: The next step up was the M1 Pro. It had up to 10 CPU cores and up to a 16-core GPU, with up to 32 GB of unified memory. Apple remarked the performance and graphics were both twice as fast as on the M1. We found it to be considerably more capable than the base chip, making it ideal for anyone who works heavily on MacBooks for music production or photo and video editing. Only the 2021 MacBook Pro (14-inch and 16-inch) used this chip.

M1 Max: Like the M1 Pro, the M1 Max had a 10-core CPU but a heftier 32-core GPU (with support for up to 64 GB of unified memory). Apple remarked it was four times faster than the M1 for graphics. As testing revealed, this chip was extremely powerful and handled every heavy-duty task with ease. It was the go-to choice if you needed a computer that could handle multiple streams of 8K or 4K video footage, 3D rendering, or app development and demos. You probably already knew whether you needed this much power. It was available in the MacBook Pro (14-inch and 16-inch) from 2021.

M1 Ultra: The M1 Ultra was the most powerful of the M1 series. It’s two M1 Max chips connected with a technology called UltraFusion. It packs a 20-core CPU, 64-core GPU (configurable up to 128 GB of unified memory), and a 32-core neural engine—complete with seven times more transistors than the base M1. Even when newer models were available, the M1 Ultra remained powerful and a solid option for anyone who needs a heavy-duty processor for intense visuals and graphics work. It was available only on the first-generation Mac Studio.

Which MacBooks Are Compatible With macOS 27 Golden Gate?

Recent findings suggest that macOS 27 Golden Gate is the latest version of the operating system that runs on MacBooks. The enhancement focuses on beefing up Siri, now integrated into Spotlight search. It also has a dedicated Siri AI app that works more like the AI chatbots we’re all so familiar with these days. This all-encompassing perspective of Apple Intelligence is even integrated into Finder and the right-click menu.

Sources indicate that notably, macOS 27 Golden Gate is the first version to drop support for pre-2020 Macs with Intel processors. The following Mac models will receive Apple’s update to macOS 27 Golden Gate:.

The previous version of macOS is Tahoe (or macOS 26), which came out in September of 2025. The software brought a host of fresh features, including a visual redesign, a spruced-up Spotlight, and a new Games app.

Which Macs Support Apple Intelligence?

According to recent reports, apple launched the first set of Apple Intelligence features with macOS Sequoia 15.1, including Writing Tools, an overhauled Siri, Smart Replies, Mail Summaries, and Clean Up in Photos. However, Apple Intelligence is exclusive to Macs with an M-series chip. This includes the following:.

Get AppleCare+ to Protect Your Devices.

None of Apple’s MacBooks are cheap, and replacement parts are nightmarishly expensive. Since the entire computer is fully integrated into Apple’s tightly designed aluminum chassis, you’re one coffee spill away from a shockingly large repair bill. This makes AppleCare+ worth buying. Remember, you have to purchase it within 60 days of buying your MacBook.

Sources indicate that apple offers monthly or yearly payments. Both include unlimited accidental protection along with 24/7 telephone support. If your MacBook has screen or enclosure damage, you’ll pay a $99 service fee; other accidental damage costs $299. The monthly payments vary depending on the specific MacBook you buy:.

Take Advantage of Apple’s Education Discounts.

According to recent reports, apple always offers small discounts on hardware for students and teachers. To access the deals, purchase through Apple’s Education Store, choose the product you want (you should see the discounted pricing), and place the order as you normally would. You don’t need to show proof that you’re a student at the time of purchase, but be honest, as Apple can ask for verification later. It’s worth noting that the discounts are not as good as what you’ll find on Amazon and sometimes at other retailers like Walmart, so be sure to check prices.

You have to be very careful when shopping for older MacBooks. Don’t get me wrong: Since the introduction of Apple Silicon in 2020, almost every MacBook Air and MacBook Pro has been a really good laptop. Never buy a MacBook that predates 2020, regardless of how cheap it is. Trust me.

It has been revealed that but even buying an older Apple Silicon model requires a discerning eye. Most older generations of MacBooks are sold only refurbished or secondhand, which adds risk. Meanwhile, prices on refurbished models fluctuate frequently, so you’ll need to watch prices closely to get the best deal. Apple’s own refurbished store prices are often higher than buying fresh models from third-party retailers like Amazon or Best Buy, but you do get some protection as they come with an Apple warranty. However, third-party retailers are always less risky than buying used on a secondhand market like Facebook Marketplace or eBay.

With that in mind, here are the older MacBooks you might see for sale, and whether I’d recommend buying.

MacBook Pro (M5): Apple doesn’t sell this one anymore, but some retailers are selling it at a discount for $1,799. That’s for 16 GB of RAM and a terabyte of storage. Since it’s nearly identical to the newer M6 MacBook Pro, except for a small performance bump, it’s a really good deal right now. I’d still say most people are better off getting a 15-inch MacBook Air because it’s cheaper and thinner, but if you want the better Mini-LED display, the M5 MacBook Pro is a solid choice right now.

MacBook Air (M4): The previous-generation MacBook Air is a fantastic laptop, but it’s no longer being sold newly introduced. However, you can now buy it refurbished for under $1,000. This configuration only comes with 256 GB of storage, though, and I don’t think it’s cheap enough to be worth it compared to the M5 model.

Sources indicate that macBook Air (M3): This one isn’t being sold upcoming anymore, and the refurbished models I could find weren’t any cheaper than the M4 MacBook Air. Just stick with the M4.

MacBook Air (M2): With the launch of the MacBook Neo, there’s really no reason to buy an older MacBook Air with only 8 GB of RAM—especially at this price.

MacBook Air (M1): Thanks to the Neo, refurbished M1 MacBook Air models have sunk to pretty dramatic lows. You can currently buy a refurbished M1 for around $400. While the M1 MacBook Air gets you a backlit keyboard, the newly introduced MacBook Neo is certainly the more handsome and portable of the two. Still, if you need something fairly limited and are willing to risk buying refurbished, I can see why an Apple Silicon MacBook for less than $400 has its appeal.

MacBook Pro (14-inch, M4): This is no longer being sold upcoming, but you can buy the refurbished model for $1,499. Earlier this year, you could have bought the M5 model for less than this. Sigh. Even still—definitely not worth it.

MacBook Pro (M3 Pro or M3 Max): Given how low the prices have dropped, these refurbished models may be worth considering, particularly for people who want a bit more performance than they’d get from a MacBook Air.

Sources indicate that at this point, I do not recommend buying refurbished MacBook Pros from the M2 or M1 generation. I haven’t seen deals strong enough to justify buying something that old.

In a recent development, there are plenty of MacBook accessories to enhance your experience, including cases and chargers for on-the-go and peripherals for your desk. Below, I’ve highlighted some of my top recommendations, but you can find more in my Best MacBook Accessories guide.

WIRED Reviews Editor Les Shu also uses this with his M4 MacBook Air and is generally a fan of Bellroy’s build quality. Amazon warns that this is a frequently returned item, but I still recommend it.

Plugable USB-C Hub Multiport Adapter for $50: If you’re buying a MacBook Air, you’ll likely need a port adapter or hub at some point. The Plugable USB-C Hub Multiport Adapter is the best I’ve tested, offering nearly every port you could need, plus enough power delivery to charge almost any MacBook. The metal chassis is a great match for the MacBook’s look, too.

Dell 27 Plus 4K for $300: Still think 4K monitors are expensive? This fantastic option from Dell stomps those myths out of existence. It has a clean aesthetic, great image quality, and even a 120-Hz refresh rate. That’s why the Dell 27 Plus 4K (9/10, WIRED Recommends) is the top pick in my Best Monitors guide. BenQ 5K Monitor (MA270S) for $1,000: If you own a MacBook Pro and need a monitor that can match the colors and sharpness of that screen, this BenQ monitor is right up your alley. If you’re a content creator, photographer, or video editor, this is one of the very best options out there.

GTA hasn't gone to space (yet), but these sci-fi games can offer you a life of crime among the stars

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1287 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time.
  • In a recent development, to this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs).
  • In a recent development, the frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time. Great news for gamers, but what about sci-fi fans?

In a recent development, to this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs). It doesn't seem likely they'll journey to the stars anytime soon — you can't really do cutting societal satire about space — but that doesn't mean there aren't GTA-adjacent sci-fi adventures set in outer space.

In a recent development, the frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet. Non-linear games set in outer space tend to be either too ambitious, like No Man's Sky, or too focused on specific experiences like space combat, like Star Wars: Squadrons.

The end result is a roster of great sandboxes that let us journey to different star systems, but no game that dares to explore a criminal fantasy with the level of depth and opportunities seen in the last few Rockstar games.

With newly introduced hardware powering far more complex open-world games, it's only a matter of time before "GTA in space" is a real thing. For now, there are some space games that let us explore sci-fi worlds, roleplaying as criminals and outlaws amongst the stars.

Massive space RPGs like Starfield and The Outer Worlds 2 offer vast playgrounds you can explore and redefine through your actions. The lawful path is the obvious choice if you'd like to save the galaxy, but a life of crime awaits those who tire of the heroics.

Starfield even has a "latest game plus" mechanic baked into the player's journey, encouraging experimentation and living different lives, so if you stick with the divisive space RPG, the criminal life is all but unavoidable. And in traditional Bethesda fashion, you're not rushed to the next "main" objective, so if you want to become the most dangerous space criminal in the Settled Systems, you'll be supported by the mechanics and systems. You can always get back to saving the galaxy when you feel like it.

The Outer Worlds 2 is another option if you want to become a star-surfing scoundrel. It might not be as absurdly expansive as Starfield, but Obsidian's whole deal has always been freedom of choice and roleplaying, so you can bet this humorous sequel also lets the protagonist become a bit of an a-hole. The main story already sets you in a collision course with corporate interests, too. Like in Mass Effect and other classic space RPGs, it's your choice to be either a goody-two-shoes or an edgy maniac, and I won't lie: the second option is usually more entertaining.

Last but not least, there's a third game that also has enough going on to support a GTA-inspired fantasy in outer space: No Man's Sky.

In a recent development, it's grown so much over the years that its original space exploration premise has been buried by content like fully customizable space stations, actual cities and towns with alien NPCs, gigantic kaiju-like beasts, and... fishing. The endless free updates have pushed the roleplaying aspects deeper, as Hello Games are really making it the "forever" space game.

Most importantly though, you can be the greatest bad guy the virtually infinite universe has ever seen, controlling entire pirate fleets and firing on (or stealing) every spaceship that you come across. It might be a bit aimless for some, but if you love a "forever game" then NMS can be the biggest space-set criminal sim ever created.

Though it took too long, Star Wars has gotten really close to cracking the GTA formula in outer space in a shameless enough way. 2024's Star Wars Outlaws is, to this date, the closest thing we've received to a space-set sandbox directly inspired by Rockstar's huge hits.

Sources indicate that by letting us fully embrace the Han Solo-like scoundrel fantasy, Massive Entertainment delivered a Star Wars adventure that's all about breaking the law. Hell, they even got a wanted system in there that has protagonist Kay Vess dodging stormtroopers and rival criminal factions like you would in Vice City.

Star Wars Outlaws' take on GTA isn't just about the surface-level gameplay and open structure; it also understands much of its playful tone, moral ambiguity, and stressful rhythm. Jumping between several medium-sized maps set on different planets and spaceship sections breaks up the experience a little, so it never quite reaches that level of seamless immersion, but if anyone wants to do a focused version of GTA in space in the future, Massive's attempt is the one game that got at least halfway there.

Before we go (and before you go back to playing GTA VI), we should remember the daring video games that, for a variety of reasons, never got to realize their visions of a crime-oriented space adventure.

In a recent development, remember Star Wars 1313 and Visceral Games' cancelled project? It's hard not to spot some of their DNA surviving in Outlaws. As Luke Skywalker wisely mentioned before noping out, "No one's ever really gone." Lucasfilm loves that, and it extends to binned video games too, thankfully. Even the elusive Battlefront 3 is back from the dead now.

Bethesda also had something going at some point with "Prey 2", a bounty hunter action game set in a cyberpunk-ish alien world. Before it was canned, it dropped one of the coolest CG game trailers ever made and teased us with a Blade Runner-esque future long before Cyberpunk hit our consoles.

Sources indicate that looking at the future, Ubisoft's Beyond Good & Evil 2 wants to go big and lawless, potentially iterating on Star Wars Outlaws and other open-world crime sims. But years after its announcement and many mind-boggling development news updates, it's hard to believe it's really ever coming out. Maybe the "Before GTA VI" meme can morph into "Before BG&E2" now that Rockstar's masterpiece is finally out.

Ultimately, Rockstar is Rockstar. A one-of-a-kind megastudio with nearly unlimited resources. Trying to replicate GTA does — either on Earth or among the stars — would be an Icarus flight in the making for most studios. There are some GTA-flavored space adventures out there, as we've shown, but we're still waiting for the one. Something that matches the deep storytelling, complete freedom, and cheeky tone of Rockstar's iconic series. OK, I gotta get out of here, I'm too hip for this, I gotta play GTA VI some more.

Recent findings suggest that jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive.

#24646. This 6-million-year-old whale may have had the most crooked face in mammal history

This 6-million-year-old whale may have had the most crooked face in mammal history

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1019 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A bizarre prehistoric whale that lived roughly 6 million years ago had a face so crooked that researchers initially suspected its fossilized skull had been distorted after death.
  • In a recent development, sperm whales and pygmy sperm whales are already known for having some of the strangest head shapes among mammals.
  • Sources indicate that now, an international team of scientists has identified an extinct pygmy sperm whale species that took this unusual anatomy to an entirely new level.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A bizarre prehistoric whale that lived roughly 6 million years ago had a face so crooked that researchers initially suspected its fossilized skull had been distorted after death. Instead, its extraordinary shape was completely natural and may represent the most extreme facial asymmetry ever documented in a mammal.

In a recent development, sperm whales and pygmy sperm whales are already known for having some of the strangest head shapes among mammals. While most vertebrates have bodies and skulls that are roughly symmetrical on both sides, toothed whales have evolved uneven skull structures to accommodate specialized organs responsible for producing sound and navigating through echolocation.

Sources indicate that now, an international team of scientists has identified an extinct pygmy sperm whale species that took this unusual anatomy to an entirely new level. Named Scaphokogia huachafo, the whale lived during the Late Miocene, between 6.3 and 5.6 million years ago, and measured approximately 2.7 meters in length. Its fossilized skull displays the most extreme facial asymmetry known in any whale or dolphin, and possibly in any mammal.

A Prehistoric Whale With an Extraordinary Skull.

Sources indicate that "Cranial asymmetry in toothed whales is directly linked to the development of fatty structures in the forehead that are involved in sound production. But in Scaphokogia huachafo, this asymmetry went far beyond the area around the blowhole. Both bony nostrils are shifted entirely to the left side of the skull, while the facial bones differ dramatically in size and position. The skull looks completely crooked," explains Aldo Benites-Palomino, lead author of the study.

It has been revealed that benites-Palomino investigated the fossil during his doctoral research at the University of Zurich's Department of Paleontology. He is currently an assistant professor at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU).

The whale's extraordinary appearance also inspired its scientific name. The word huachafo comes from Peruvian Spanish and is commonly used to describe something excessively flashy, bizarre, extravagant, or even tacky.

"In Peru, huachafo is an everyday word for anything that is flashy, over-the-top, bizarre, extravagant or difficult to categorize aesthetically," notes Benites-Palomino.

In a recent development, "When we looked at the proportions of this whale - with its face strongly shifted to the left and its oversized, downward-curving snout - it broke every rule of symmetry and elegance seen in living cetaceans. Its anatomy is so extravagant and odd that huachafo seemed the perfect name for it.".

Scientists Initially Suspected the Skull Was Deformed.

The remarkable fossil was originally recovered during the mid-1990s from the Pisco Formation in southern Peru. This desert region is famous among paleontologists for its exceptionally preserved fossils of ancient marine animals.

Benites-Palomino first encountered the specimen in 2015 while preparing his Bachelor's thesis at the Museo de Historia Natural in Lima. Its dramatically uneven shape immediately raised an important question: Was the skull genuinely this crooked when the whale was alive, or had millions of years of geological pressure distorted it?

"The initial suspicion with skulls this distorted is always taphonomy - that the specimen may have been flattened or twisted by sediment pressure over millions of years," says Benites-Palomino.

"But the sutures are fully closed, and there are no fractures, pathologies or deformations elsewhere on the skull. This was genuine biology, not a result of poor preservation.".

The findings confirmed that the extraordinary asymmetry was part of the whale's natural anatomy, rather than damage caused by burial, fossilization, or disease.

A Bizarre Adaptation for Hunting Along the Seafloor.

The whale's unusual skull also offers clues about how it survived. Modern sperm whales typically pursue squid in deep ocean waters, but Scaphokogia huachafo appears to have followed a very different hunting strategy. Its anatomy suggests that it was highly adapted to searching for food along the bottom of shallow coastal waters.

One of its most distinctive features was a large, tube-shaped snout strengthened by dense bone and cartilage that had hardened into bone. These heavy structures served as natural ballast, moving the whale's center of gravity forward and downward.

In a recent development, its snout also pointed downward at an angle of 31 degrees relative to the rest of its skull. By reconstructing the joint connecting the skull to the first neck vertebra, known as the atlas, scientists determined that Scaphokogia could bend its head downward by as much as 55 degrees.

"The entire cranio-cervical complex is modified to point the snout directly toward the bottom," explains Gabriel Aguirre-Fernández, co-author of the study and doctoral advisor at the University of Zurich.

"The combination of dense bone, the downward-curving snout and the flexible neck articulation allowed the animal to move directly above the seabed and feed close to the sediment.".

In a recent development, researchers also believe the whale may have relied on its highly specialized echolocation system to locate prey beneath the soft sediment of coastal environments. Unlike other marine mammals that forage along the ocean floor, Scaphokogia lacked the sensitive facial whiskers or specialized visual adaptations that can help animals find food near the bottom.

Instead, its extraordinarily asymmetrical skull may have supported a sophisticated biological sonar system that allowed it to detect hidden prey.

It has been revealed that this unusual feeding strategy represents a specialized way of life that no longer exists among modern marine mammals. As ocean conditions shifted toward the end of the Miocene, the ecological niche occupied by Scaphokogia disappeared, eventually giving way to the marine mammal communities familiar today.

The discovery provides a remarkable glimpse into how far evolution once pushed the anatomy of whales, producing a creature whose dramatically crooked face was not a deformity, but an adaptation to a vanished underwater world.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that three men are vying for one of the most powerful positions in sports when delegates from more than 200 member nations of FIFA, soccer's global governing body, cast their ballots at the FIFA presidential election, to be held in Rabat on March 18, 2027. DW looks at the field of candidates.

In a recent development, gianni Infantino was first elected FIFA president in February 2016, promising greater transparency and a fresh start in the wake of the corruption scandals that marked the Sepp Blatter era. Under Infantino's leadership, FIFA's revenues have continued to grow, the Club World Cup has been revamped, and the men's World Cup has been expanded to include 48 teams.

Industry observers note that during his decade in office, the 56-year-old Swiss has built a global network of support. Infantino enjoys significant backing in Africa, South America, and large parts of Asia — a result of multi-billion-dollar development programs and financial grants provided to national associations. Many smaller member associations view him as a president who takes their interests more seriously than his predecessors did.

At the same time, critics accuse Infantino of consolidating power within the organization around himself. During his tenure, oversight and control bodies have been restructured multiple times, and key positions have been filled with his own loyalists.

Industry observers note that infantino's ostentatious closeness to political leaders has also sparked debate — whether exemplified by his conduct during the World Cup in Qatar, his tight ties to Saudi Arabia or his public appearances alongside US President Donald Trump (though that relationship is remarked to have cooled significantly after the 2026 World Cup). Detractors accuse him of seeking proximity to authoritarian rulers and intermingling political interests too closely with football.

A failed initiative to grant private investors a larger stake in lucrative FIFA competitions (FIFA Forward Enterprise) has also placed Infantino under considerable pressure. As the FIFA election approaches, he faces the prospect of legal challenges; European football's governing body UEFA is aiming to take action over the investment plan, while other critics are calling for an investigation by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

However, his time in office has brought many of FIFA's 211 member associations additional development funding and other revenue. This makes him the man to beat in the March vote.

In a recent development, philippe Diallo is Europe's candidate. The 63-year-old, who was elected president of the French Football Federation in 2023, is seen as an experienced sports administrator with a pragmatic and measured leadership style.

He has the backing of UEFA, as well as many of its 55 member associations, including the German Football Association (DEB).

"Philippe Diallo stands for a version of football that embraces responsibility and tackles future challenges with determination," DFB President Bernd Neuendorf stated in a statement announcing the German FA's position.

"We want a FIFA that serves the sport in the interest of all its member associations. That is why we support Philippe Diallo with great conviction.".

Diallo is positioning himself as a clear alternative to Infantino. His supporters see him as a candidate who stands for sound leadership, transparency, and a stronger dialogue with member associations. Unlike the incumbent, however, he lacks a global network of allies.

The third man in the race is Kozo Tashima. The 68-year-old was president of the Japan Football Association (JFA) from 2016 to 2024 and has been one of the most influential officials in Asia for decades.

During a press conference in the Japanese capital Tokyo on Friday, Tashima mentioned the words "integrity, fairness, trust and transparency" several times in explaining his decision to run.

"I just don't only want to be the FIFA president, my intention is to make FIFA better," he stated.

It has been revealed that "Being the president is the shortcut to making that happen. I just want to clean up the federation and make it a fair organization. I want to help rebuild the whole organization.".

Tashima also acknowledged that failing to have won the endorsement of any of the regional confederations — the Asian Football Confederation is supporting Infantino — makes him a longshot to win the election.

It has been revealed that but he could still play a key role in the outcome. At a press conference on Tuesday, Diallo mentioned he intended to reach out to Tashima to "unite forces" to defeat Infantino. Tashima hasn't ruled out the notion.

"We do share some moral or ethical positions, so he's a great person to team up with," he remarked.

"Diallo is also very strict in governance and he does have a lot of experience in management," he added.

However, Tashima also noted that he hadn't had any thoughts of withdrawing from the race.

If Infantino's challengers do manage to join forces in some way, they might just stand a chance of upsetting the highly favored incumbent.

Tech Report: The Stormy Southwest Pacific

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tropical Cyclone Xavier rolled out the basin’s storm season with a bang.
  • Even as the unusually quiet 2026 storm season winds down in the North Atlantic, seas have begun to stir on the other side of the world in the Southwest Pacific.
  • Named Xavier, the system intensified rapidly, thriving in an environment with minimal wind shear and sea surface temperatures of 29 degrees Celsius (84 degrees Fahrenheit)—well above the threshold required to sustain and strengthen developing tropical cyclones.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tropical Cyclone Xavier rolled out the basin’s storm season with a bang.

Even as the unusually quiet 2026 storm season winds down in the North Atlantic, seas have begun to stir on the other side of the world in the Southwest Pacific. On November 15, 2026, the Fiji Meteorological Service began issuing updates about a slow-moving tropical disturbance northeast of Samoa and the Cook Islands. Within just a few days, it had become one of the most intense November tropical cyclones the region has seen in decades.

Named Xavier, the system intensified rapidly, thriving in an environment with minimal wind shear and sea surface temperatures of 29 degrees Celsius (84 degrees Fahrenheit)—well above the threshold required to sustain and strengthen developing tropical cyclones. Xavier was the basin’s second named storm of the season, following only Wati, a short-lived storm that emerged in October.

As Xavier developed, NASA satellite data highlighted the storm churning along the southwestern edge of a massive tongue of warm water spanning from the west coast of South America to the central Pacific—a telltale sign of the El Niño that has been present in the region since June.

It has been revealed that when the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) on NASA’s Aqua satellite captured this image at 02:53 Universal Time on November 17, 2026 (4:53 p.m. Cook Islands Time on November 16), forecasters estimated Xavier had maximum winds of about 195 kilometers (120 miles) per hour. Winds reached a peak intensity of 220 kilometers (140 miles) per hour later that day, a Category 5 storm on the cyclone intensity scale used in the region or a Category 4 on the Saffir-Simpson scale.

According to recent reports, the storm ranks as the strongest November tropical cyclone east of the international date line on record, noted Colorado State University hurricane expert Phil Klotzbach. Xavier’s formation east of the date line, near the northern Cook Islands, was unusual, but its easterly position aligns with research that indicates that storm activity in the region typically shifts northeast during El Niño years. Research also demonstrates that El Niño tends to fuel storms that strengthen at an unusually rapid pace.

Recent findings suggest that according to news reports, Xavier damaged homes and caused power disruptions as it passed the northern Cook Islands. It then encountered dry air and a less favorable wind shear environment and slowly weakened as it pushed westward, reducing the threat that it posed to Samoa and American Samoa.

Sources indicate that xavier is likely one of the first of several storms to affect the region in the coming months. A seasonal outlook from the Fiji Meteorological Service projects that the region could see between 11 and 15 named tropical cyclones this season, with the greatest risk east of the international date line. Storm activity in the Southwest Pacific basin typically peaks in February.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material.

Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with looks to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water, construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals.

However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment.

According to recent reports, two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics, the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon.

It has been revealed that in addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies.

"With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the significant infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz remarked in a statement. "That shouldn't be the Wild West.".

Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.

A 3-million-year-old child just made human evolution far more complicated

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (740 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A century after the Taung Child transformed our understanding of where humans came from, scientists are discovering that this famous fossil still has surprises to reveal.
  • The international study was led by Professor Gabriele Macho of the Archaeology, Environmental Changes and Geo-Chemistry (AMGC) research group at Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB).
  • First discovered in South Africa in 1924, the Taung Child provided the first concrete evidence supporting the African origins of humanity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A century after the Taung Child transformed our understanding of where humans came from, scientists are discovering that this famous fossil still has surprises to reveal. A new study published in Nature dates the ancient remains to between 2.96 and 3.03 million years ago and suggests that the human family tree in southern Africa was much more complicated than previously believed.

The international study was led by Professor Gabriele Macho of the Archaeology, Environmental Changes and Geo-Chemistry (AMGC) research group at Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB). The findings challenge long-standing assumptions about how early human relatives evolved and how different species were related.

First discovered in South Africa in 1924, the Taung Child provided the first concrete evidence supporting the African origins of humanity. It also became the original "type specimen" used to define the species Australopithecus africanus. However, scientists never established definitive criteria for assigning later fossil discoveries to this species. As a result, the Taung Child remains the only fossil that can be identified with certainty as Australopithecus africanus.

"For over 100 years, we assumed the Taung Child was just one of many similar fossils from the era," indicates Professor Gabriele Macho. "Our findings turn that on its head. The human family tree wasn't a neat, straight trunk -- it was a chaotic, tangled bush driven by climate shifts.".

Ancient Fossils Reveal a More Complex Human Family Tree.

To investigate how the Taung Child compared with other early human relatives, researchers examined tooth structure and patterns of brain and dental development during growth. They found that several adult fossils traditionally classified as Australopithecus africanus followed developmental patterns that differed from those of the Taung Child.

Sources indicate that differences in brain development were particularly revealing. They suggest that fossils previously grouped into a single species may actually represent several distinct hominin species that inhabited the Sterkfontein region, either at the same time or during different periods.

These findings raise important questions about the diversity of our ancient ancestors and suggest that early human evolution followed a much more complicated path than scientists once assumed.

How Climate Change Shaped Human Evolution.

In a recent development, the researchers believe that dramatic environmental changes played a major role in creating this evolutionary diversity. Millions of years ago, southern Africa experienced repeated shifts between wetter and drier climates, continually transforming the landscape and the habitats available to early human relatives.

As suitable environments expanded and contracted, ancient hominin populations moved with them. Some groups became geographically isolated and evolved along different paths, while others eventually came back into contact and interbred. These changing conditions also exposed populations to different predators and pathogens, creating additional pressures that shaped their evolution.

Recent findings suggest that southern Africa's position along the boundary between tropical and temperate ecosystems made it especially important in this process. Over thousands of years, shifting habitats may have repeatedly brought different hominin species together, creating opportunities for interbreeding and hybridization.

A Greener South Africa 3 Million Years Ago.

In a recent development, the study also reveals a surprising picture of the environment in which the Taung Child lived. Evidence preserved in fossilized pollen indicates that the region was once considerably wetter and more heavily forested than it is today.

Researchers identified evidence of tree species that are now found hundreds of kilometers to the northeast, suggesting that the landscape surrounding the Taung Child was dramatically different from modern South Africa.

Together, these discoveries challenge the traditional view of human evolution as a relatively straightforward progression from one species to another. Instead, they point to a shifting network of populations that repeatedly separated, adapted, reunited, and sometimes interbred as environmental conditions changed.

In a recent development, more than 100 years after its discovery, the Taung Child is once again transforming our understanding of human origins. Its latest secrets suggest that the emergence of our own genus, Homo, was preceded by a far more diverse and interconnected world of ancient human relatives than previously recognized.

  • Industry observers note that the new enterprise unit, dubbed Booking Partner Division, will combine Booking.com Strategic Partnerships with Rocket Travel by Agoda, and is set to begin operating in January.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Booking Holdings is bringing together two of its business-to-business travel operations in a upcoming division it hopes will be transformational, betting that a larger, coordinated partner platform can generate growth as artificial intelligence changes how travelers discover and book trips.

Industry observers note that the new enterprise unit, dubbed Booking Partner Division, will combine Booking.com Strategic Partnerships with Rocket Travel by Agoda, and is set to begin operating in January. Agoda CEO Omri Morgenshtern will lead the unit, which aims to help businesses such as banks, airlines and online travel companies sell trips or build branded experiences for their customers.

"We realize that if we focus our efforts both on the product side, but also on the go-to-market side, then we can potentially grow faster and serve better partners," Morgenshtern told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

He remarked existing partners will find new and better products, which will also help grow the partner base.

Sources indicate that the move gives Booking a single organization to coordinate technology, travel supply and commercial expertise across business relationships. The manufacturer says partners will be able to use its global supply and technology through white-label platforms, integrated applications, branded solutions and hotel-chain rate distribution.

The portfolio includes more than 4.7 million properties, 33 million accommodation listings, more than 500 airlines and more than 200 car rental providers, according to the manufacturer.

Competitor Expedia Group has seen notable growth by prioritizing its enterprise efforts, including a strategy rolled out in 2022 to make its technology platform available to business partners looking to add travel to their own offerings.

From 2018 to 2023, Expedia’s business-to-business revenue grew at a 16% compound annual rate, while adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, or EBITDA, for the division grew at a 28% rate, the manufacturer said in 2024.

In 2025, Expedia’s B2B revenue rose 18% to $4.8 billion, and its segment adjusted EBITDA increased 22% to $1.26 billion. Those figures represented about a third of Expedia’s total revenue and more than a third of its adjusted EBITDA for the full year.

Morgenshtern declined to say how much the upcoming division is expected to contribute to Booking Holdings' overall revenue and profit, but he noted the opportunity for growth is immense, estimating the total addressable market at $2 trillion.

Online travel agencies have been pressured this year as investors scrutinize how AI will change the way customers search for and then book their travel.

Companies that offer lodging, experiences and other travel and leisure are grappling with how to stay visible if AI tools become the newly introduced starting point for planning and reservations.

Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro remarked on the manufacturer’s earnings call Tuesday that guests already use AI to discover and initiative Disney trips, and that some are using the tools to book.

“Ultimately, we want Disney to show up in those tools,” he remarked, adding that Disney is exploring ways to let guests make reservations directly from them.

Booking anticipates offering partners AI capabilities that draw on the organization's existing travel know-how while minimizing token costs, it remarked.

"I see a lot of AI demos," Morgenshtern noted, drawing a distinction between a product that caters to a few customers and one that's scalable and works even when overloaded by travel emergencies. He said he's "super optimistic" about the bespoke product — a vertical agent — that Booking will offer to its partners.

Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer.

Explanation: On November 17, fans of interstellar spaceflight around planet Earth were invited to shine a message into the night sky. Traced by a flashlight beam switched on and off, the dashes and dots of a Morse code message captured in this time exposure from the Emirates Astronomical Observatory are read V-G-R. That's a call sign for the Voyager 1 spacecraft at the moment in interstellar space some 26 billion kilometers away. How long did it take the message to reach humanity's most distant interstellar spacecraft? Traveling at the speed of light, the answer is one day. In fact, the Voyager 1 spacecraft was confirmed to reach its one light-day distance milestone on November 18, at 10:16:07 UTC, nearly 50 years after launch in 1977. For extra credit, fans of math can calculate that at one light-day per 50 years, Voyager 1 will reach its one light-year (365 light-days) distance milestone in about 18,250 years.Tomorrow's picture: cruising.

Scientists tested 212 plant-based foods. Every single one contained fungal toxins

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1100 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every one of 212 plant-based foods and drinks tested in a newly introduced study contained at least one naturally occurring fungal toxin, raising questions about the potential health effects of regularly consuming these products.
  • In a recent development, researchers examined a wide selection of vegetarian and vegan products sold in the UK, including meat alternatives and dairy substitutes.
  • Industry observers note that mycotoxins are poisonous substances produced by certain fungi, including molds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every one of 212 plant-based foods and drinks tested in a newly introduced study contained at least one naturally occurring fungal toxin, raising questions about the potential health effects of regularly consuming these products.

In a recent development, researchers examined a wide selection of vegetarian and vegan products sold in the UK, including meat alternatives and dairy substitutes. They detected at least one of 19 mycotoxins in every product, and many contained multiple toxins.

Industry observers note that mycotoxins are poisonous substances produced by certain fungi, including molds. They can enter the food supply when agricultural crops become contaminated during growing, harvesting, or storage.

Recent findings suggest that the investigation was led by scientists at the University of Parma in Italy, with contributions from Cranfield University. The researchers analyzed 212 products, including plant-based meat alternatives (PMBAs) and plant-based beverages (PBBs). The selection covered foods commonly found on supermarket shelves, such as vegan burgers, vegetarian chicken pieces, vegan sausages, and oat, almond, and soy milk.

Industry observers note that although the findings highlight how widespread these naturally occurring contaminants can be, the researchers also identified an important reassuring detail. Every product contained mycotoxin concentrations below recommended European Union guideline levels, which the team said reflected the high food quality standards maintained by the UK food industry.

Why Plant-Based Foods Can Contain Fungal Toxins.

Recent findings suggest that many of the ingredients used to manufacture plant-based foods are particularly susceptible to fungal contamination. Grains, legumes, and seeds can encounter mold in fields or storage facilities, creating opportunities for mycotoxins to develop before the ingredients reach food manufacturers.

Recent findings suggest that unlike bacteria or viruses, mycotoxins are chemical substances produced by certain fungi. Their presence in food does not necessarily mean the product contains living mold, and detecting a toxin does not automatically mean the food is unsafe. The potential health risk depends on factors such as the type of toxin, its concentration, and how much a person consumes over time.

This distinction is especially notable for people who eat plant-based products frequently. Someone whose diet regularly includes meat substitutes, dairy alternatives, grains, and legumes may encounter these substances through several different foods rather than a single source.

Could Repeated Exposure Pose Health Risks?

While the concentrations detected in the UK products were below recommended EU guidelines, researchers say the potential effects of repeated exposure deserve closer attention.

Earlier studies have suggested that consuming small amounts of mycotoxins regularly may contribute to cumulative exposure and potentially increase health risks. In other words, assessing a single product may not provide a complete picture of a person's overall dietary exposure.

Eating one of these products occasionally is unlikely to cause problems based on the levels reported. However, a diet that relies heavily or exclusively on plant-based foods could involve repeated exposure to mycotoxins from numerous ingredients and products. Researchers say understanding the combined effects is crucial for evaluating possible long-term health consequences.

It has been revealed that the severity of mycotoxin exposure varies depending on the compounds involved and the amount consumed. At sufficiently high or harmful exposure levels, certain mycotoxins can damage the liver and kidneys, interfere with normal immune system function, and increase the risk of cancer.

The new findings do not establish that the tested products cause these conditions. Instead, they provide information that scientists can use to estimate how much exposure consumers may receive through their diets and develop more accurate food safety risk assessments for the UK population.

Scientists Call for Better Monitoring of Plant-Based Ingredients.

According to recent reports, andrea Patriarca, Senior Lecturer in Mycology at Cranfield University, emphasized that mycotoxins are a natural part of the food environment and should not discourage people from eating a varied diet. Mycology is the branch of biology devoted to studying fungi, including molds and yeasts.

"Mycotoxins occur naturally in foods and cannot be completely avoided. As consumers, we should not be frightened or deterred from enjoying a variety of products.

However, a significant concern arises when fresh foods enter the market, as there are at the moment no established regulations to monitor mycotoxins. We collaborate closely with various sectors in the food industry, from farmers to food companies, to help implement effective mycotoxin management integrated within food safety standards. The data from our research helps food safety organizations in assessing risks, particularly in complex multi-ingredient products.

Recent findings suggest that we are right now collaborating with the University of Parma to evaluate the risks faced by the population based on different dietary habits. Our aim is to advise policymakers and raise awareness among vulnerable consumers.".

According to recent reports, the researchers are particularly interested in how food safety monitoring can keep pace with the growing range of plant-based products. Foods made from multiple ingredients present additional challenges because each component may introduce different contaminants, making overall exposure more difficult to assess.

Their work also underscores the importance of monitoring raw materials throughout the food production process. Identifying and controlling contamination before ingredients are combined into finished products could help manufacturers manage potential risks more effectively.

What the Findings Mean for Plant-Based Diets.

The discovery of fungal toxins in all 212 products highlights the importance of studying dietary exposure across multiple foods, rather than evaluating each product in isolation.

For consumers, the results are not a reason to abandon vegan or vegetarian foods. The concentrations measured were below recommended EU guidelines, and the researchers stress that mycotoxins cannot be completely eliminated from the food supply.

In a recent development, instead, the study points to the need for continued research into how different eating habits influence exposure, particularly among people who depend heavily on plant-based products. The University of Parma and Cranfield University are continuing their collaboration to investigate these dietary patterns, identify potentially vulnerable groups, and provide evidence that can inform future food safety policies.

The research, titled "Mycotoxin contamination in plant-based beverages and meat alternatives: A survey of the UK market," was published in the journal Food Control.

The study was conducted as part of the European Union-funded Horizon Europe FunShield4Med project (HORIZON-WIDERA-2021-ACCESS-03), Grant Agreement No 101079173.

Myanmar genocide ruling: Rohingya say struggle for justice not over

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The International Court of Justice (ICJ) on Thursday ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the country's Rohingya community a decade ago, in a historic judgment hailed by the long-persecuted minority and rights groups.
  • The United Nations' top court also ordered the Myanmar government to prevent a repeat of the crimes, undertake legal reforms to protect the Rohingya and provide the victims with reparations or, where it cannot, compensate them.
