After 8 years in space, a groundbreaking X-ray telescope finally opens its eyes

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1616 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that after eight years in space and a journey covering 10 billion kilometers, a pioneering X-ray telescope traveling to Mercury has captured its first observations of a distant cosmic object.
  • According to recent reports, scientists at the University of Leicester are now evaluating the Mercury Imaging X-ray Spectrometer (MIXS), which is traveling aboard the two-spacecraft mission.
  • The telescope has spent eight years traveling through space, making it essential to confirm that its delicate components are still working properly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that after eight years in space and a journey covering 10 billion kilometers, a pioneering X-ray telescope traveling to Mercury has captured its first observations of a distant cosmic object. The instrument, built in the UK, successfully detected X-rays from the Crab Nebula, one of the brightest X-ray sources in the sky, marking an vital milestone for the European Space Agency (ESA) and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency's BepiColombo mission.

According to recent reports, scientists at the University of Leicester are now evaluating the Mercury Imaging X-ray Spectrometer (MIXS), which is traveling aboard the two-spacecraft mission. Their initial results are highly encouraging, arriving just as BepiColombo prepares to enter orbit around Mercury on November 21.

The telescope has spent eight years traveling through space, making it essential to confirm that its delicate components are still working properly. Although engineers monitored MIXS throughout the journey, the instrument could not look directly into space until September. That opportunity came after the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) separated from the two science orbiters, the Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and Mercury Magnetosphere Orbiter (MMO) or Mio.

With its view finally unobstructed, MIXS could begin the critical tests needed before the spacecraft enters its planned orbit around the solar system's smallest planet.

A Telescope's First Look Across 6,500 Light-Years.

For its first astronomical target, the team selected the Crab Nebula, located approximately 6,500 light-years from Earth. This well-studied remnant of an exploded star produces a strong, predictable X-ray signal, making it an ideal reference for testing the telescope's performance.

Sources indicate that by examining how MIXS observes this distant object, researchers can determine whether the instrument still performs as expected after its lengthy journey. They can also compare the results with laboratory measurements collected in 2015, when the telescope was last tested on Earth.

According to recent reports, the main observation campaign took place on September 11 and 12. Over 39 hours, the spacecraft carried out 55 carefully controlled changes in orientation to collect the data.

Recent findings suggest that one important measurement was the telescope's angular resolution, which describes its ability to distinguish small details in an image. Scientists determined this by examining how widely the Crab Nebula's X-ray signal spread across the detector. Remarkably, MIXS delivered slightly sharper resolution than it had during its laboratory tests in 2015.

That improvement is particularly encouraging because the instrument will eventually use its X-ray vision to investigate the composition of Mercury's surface.

Better Than Expected After Eight Years in Space.

Professor Emma Bunce, Principal Investigator (PI) for MIXS and Director of the Institute for Space at the University of Leicester, welcomed the results as a major achievement for the international team responsible for developing the instrument.

Recent findings suggest that professor Bunce mentioned: "We have waited a long time to make measurements with MIXS and it is fantastic to see it operating brilliantly in space. This is testament to our engineering and technical team, and our international partners who we have worked with over many years to build this incredible instrument. 80% of the technology on MIXS is new!

Recent findings suggest that "During our calibration observations we have determined that MIXS is generally performing fantastically well in space! We have no effects in our images that are associated with 'stray light' (optical photons getting in when they should not). We continue to see effects of galactic cosmic rays as we did during cruise, but we understand these and can filter them out. We see some self-fluorescence which appears when the Sun is illuminating the optic, but this won't affect our dayside observations of Mercury's surface. And the detector has suffered no radiation damage after 8 years in space.

"We see some effects in the instrument that we are still studying and expect to undertake some optimization procedures during the Mercury commissioning phase to fine tune MIXS in preparation for the science phase.".

The results suggest that the telescope has weathered its long exposure to the harsh space environment exceptionally well. Engineers have found no unwanted visible light interfering with its images, and the effects of high-energy cosmic rays are understood well enough to be removed during data processing.

According to recent reports, the team has also identified a small amount of X-ray emission originating within the instrument itself when sunlight strikes its optics. However, this effect is not expected to interfere with observations of Mercury's sunlit surface. Most importantly, the detector demonstrates no signs of radiation damage after eight years in space.

Some remaining effects still require investigation, and scientists expect to make further adjustments after the spacecraft reaches Mercury to ensure that MIXS is ready for its full scientific mission.

How X-Rays Will Reveal Mercury's Hidden Chemistry.

BepiColombo is designed to investigate Mercury in unprecedented detail. As the smallest and one of the least explored rocky planets in our solar system, Mercury offers scientists a rare opportunity to understand how planets form and change under the extreme conditions found close to a star.

According to recent reports, one of the mission's major goals is to uncover the planet's chemical composition and geological history. These findings could help explain Mercury's unusual characteristics while providing broader insights into the formation and evolution of the solar system.

Industry observers note that MIXS, carried aboard the Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO), will play a central role in this investigation. Developed by a European consortium led by the University of Leicester, it draws on the university's long history of X-ray astronomy research.

It is the first imaging X-ray telescope to operate on a planetary science mission. Working alongside other scientific instruments, MIXS will help produce a global map showing the elements that make up Mercury's surface, revealing its atomic composition in greater detail than ever before. It is also the only UK-led scientific instrument aboard BepiColombo and receives support from the UK Space Agency.

In a recent development, the instrument works by detecting fluorescent X-rays released by rocks on Mercury's surface. When powerful X-rays from the Sun strike these rocks, they can cause atoms within the material to emit X-rays of their own. Different elements produce characteristic X-ray signals, allowing scientists to identify what the surface is made of without collecting physical samples.

MIXS will make these measurements with assistance from the Solar Intensity X-ray and particle Spectrometer (SIXS), which monitors the solar radiation and particles reaching Mercury.

Sources indicate that the telescope will also examine X-rays emitted from Mercury's nighttime surface when charged particles associated with the planet's magnetic environment strike it. These measurements could reveal important connections between Mercury's surface and the surrounding space environment.

A 10 Billion Kilometer Journey With a Personal Legacy.

Sources indicate that for Dr. Adrian Martindale, MIXS Instrument Scientist at the University of Leicester's School of Physics and Astronomy, the successful observations represent the culmination of more than two decades of work.

Martindale joined the project in 2003 while still an undergraduate student and has been involved in nearly every aspect of the instrument's development.

Dr. Martindale said: "BepiColombo, and MIXS in particular, are like part of my family. I've been involved since I was an undergraduate and touched almost every part of the instrument before it was launched.

In a recent development, "This first data is mind-blowing to me. The last time we could see through this telescope it was in the basement under the School of Physics and Astronomy in Leicester, but after a rocket launch, eight years in space and 10 billion kilometers traveled it looks just the same. I can't wait to see the science data it produces when we get into orbit.".

The milestone also carries special meaning for the team because MIXS represents the scientific legacy of Professor George Fraser. Fraser was the instrument's original Principal Investigator and the driving force behind its innovative optical design before his death in March 2014.

Professor Bunce added: "We are thinking of George as we operate MIXS fully in space for the first time and know that he would be very, very proud of the team and delighted at our first light observations.".

BepiColombo Prepares for Its Final Arrival at Mercury.

BepiColombo began its arrival phase on September 3, when the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) separated from the spacecraft assembly.

The remaining connected spacecraft are scheduled to enter orbit around Mercury on November 21. The two science orbiters, MPO and Mio, are then expected to separate on December 9 to 10, allowing them to prepare for their respective scientific operations.

It has been revealed that the mission's primary science phase is scheduled to begin in April 2027. Once underway, BepiColombo will investigate Mercury's surface, internal structure, magnetic field, and surrounding environment, helping scientists piece together the history of a planet that remains surprisingly mysterious despite its proximity to the Sun.

For the MIXS team, the successful first observations of the Crab Nebula offer an early indication of what the instrument may accomplish when it finally turns its attention to Mercury.

International Collaboration and Funding.

MIXS was developed through a partnership involving research institutions and technology companies across Europe. Participating organizations include:.

UK funding for the BepiColombo MIXS instrument comes from the UK Space Agency, which serves as the lead funding organization, along with STFC, the European Space Agency, and the University of Leicester.

Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (787 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, another crucial opposition media outlet in Turkey has been placed under state control.
  • A trustee has also been appointed: The state deposit protection fund, TMSF, which usually administers the assets of insolvent companies, has been put in charge.
  • Industry observers note that A large police contingent raided the broadcaster's headquarters in Istanbul, with counterterrorism officers searching the offices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, another crucial opposition media outlet in Turkey has been placed under state control. On Tuesday morning, authorities raided the offices of the television broadcaster Sozcu TV and the news portal Sozcu.com.tr, and arrested several executives.

A trustee has also been appointed: The state deposit protection fund, TMSF, which usually administers the assets of insolvent companies, has been put in charge. Sozcu was one of the last big media companies in Turkey to regularly report critically on the government of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

Industry observers note that A large police contingent raided the broadcaster's headquarters in Istanbul, with counterterrorism officers searching the offices. According to Sozcu, its chairwoman, Funda Tuncer Sidali, and Asim Akgul, the former chief executive of the Sozcu group, were among those arrested.

The broadcaster did not initially announce the appointment of the trustee on its digital channels. It did call on its audience to follow it under a new account. The leader of the main opposition party, Ozgur Ozel, declared on X: "You will never be able to prevent this nation's voice from rising, its rebellion from being heard, its cry from echoing.".

It has been revealed that the Istanbul public prosecutor's office has confirmed the arrangements. It justified the investigation with claims of a suspected connection between the owner of Sozcu, Burak Akhay, and the Gülen movement. The Turkish government blames this movement, which was once allied to Erdogan, for the attempted coup in 2016, and has designated it a terrorist organization.

In a recent development, according to the investigators, Akbay is remarked to have used foreign bank accounts to finance two companies involved in media activities on behalf of the Gülen movement. They claim there is strong suspicion that he was able, in this way, to hold a leadership position in the organization.

In a recent development, it is not fresh for the Turkish state to take over media organizations by appointing trustees. Many media companies accused of being close to the Gülen movement were brought under state control in this way after the attempted coup in 2016. What is new is that for about a year now this is also happening to media seen as pro-opposition.

It has been revealed that sozcu is not the first opposition broadcaster to be targeted by the authorities. The TELEI TV channel was searched on October 24, 2025. Its editor-in-chief, Merdan Yanardag, was arrested on charges of espionage and remains in custody. The offices of Halk TV were raided on October 14 this year. There, too, a trustee was put in charge.

Industry observers note that in the space of just over a year, three of the most important opposition television channels have been brought under state control. Observers see this as another step toward an increasingly authoritarian and politically isolated system.

Berk Esen, a political scientist with Sabanci University in Istanbul, sees these measures as a significant weakening of the opposition in the public domain.

Esen told DW that the government may first have acted behind the scenes and tried to bring Sozcu to heel politically. When this didn't succeed, it invoked the judiciary. Esen notes Turkey is increasingly moving toward an authoritarian system. The attempt to prevent opposition organizations and media from gaining strength and influence is part of this.

Industry observers note that esen describes the opposition's success in local government elections in March 2024 as a political turning point. Since then, he claims, the government has seen its chances of winning political competitions at the ballot box receding. "It's become harder for the AKP to win elections," says Esen. "That's why it's attacking the opposition and the free media both at once.".

Several opposition mayors have also been arrested in recent months and replaced by trustees. They include the mayor of Istanbul and presidential candidate Ekrem Imamoglu, who has been in detention since his arrest in March last year. He is regarded as one of Erdogan's most promising challengers.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that the Turkish Journalists' Association (TGC) spoke of a "black winter for press freedom," and unveiled its solidarity with all those affected. It described the recent developments as a serious attack on press freedom. The fact that a trustee had been appointed, first at Halk TV and now at Sozcu, showed how the media climate in Turkey has deteriorated, it said.

"These days, too, shall pass," the TGC declared. "When that day comes, those journalists who seek the truth today will be remembered, as will the decisions that prevent the public from hearing that truth.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the past few years, WIRED has tested nearly every major brand of essential oil diffuser. Pura’s been our top nebulizer-style device (these work by blowing air through oil) for years due to its ease of use and sprawling library of high-end scents.

In fact, no brand even comes close to Pura's sheer breadth of available fragrances—with more than 150 options from big names like Anthropologie, Nest, LAFCO, Brooklyn Candle Company, Studio McGee, and more. Pura even has special seasonal collabs, like this month’s Nutcracker-inspired scents from the Fresh York City Ballet. These diffusers are also highly convenient to use in that you can control them from your phone via an app (the Home, Plus, and Car also have buttons on the actual devices).

But, it's a luxury you'll pay for. If you own a Pura or have seen it in stores, you already know the scents aren't cheap; single cartridges range from $14 for Pura’s house line all the way up to $21 for name brands like Thymes and Votivo. (The prices displayed on Pura's website look lower, but that's only if you buy a recurring subscription—make sure you note the one-time purchase price.).

It has been revealed that cartridges can last for a month or more in the Pura Mini, but in a larger diffuser like the Pura Plus, they may only last a couple of weeks. That's why the best time to stock up on scents for the year is during a sale, like Pura’s Cyber Week event. Right now through December 6, all fragrances are 20 percent off, and all diffusers are 30 percent off.

Recent findings suggest that pura's diffuser lineup isn't perfect, but neither are any of the diffusers we've tried from any brand. Diffusers can be loud or messy, take up a lot of space, or have an uninspiring line of scents. Pura's Mini and Car models are worthwhile yet quirky (though I can't recommend the Plus), but the Home has given me no concerns in six months of testing.

If you're in the market for a Pura diffuser, our top pick for most people is the upcoming Pura Home. The first Pura I ever owned was the 3 model, and I've also had the 4, but the 5 (rebranded “Home”) improves on just about everything, with dual-band (2.4 GHz and 5.0 GHz) Wi-Fi compatibility; faster diffusion; control buttons on the device itself; and even a new way to load cartridges, where you can slide out the bottom portion (which is flat to sit on a surface), seat the scents, and click it into place. QR codes on the cartridges inform your app which scents they are and when they were loaded, so it can, in turn, remind you when it's time to replace them. I also like that this model is totally silent.

Sources indicate that I also recommend the oval-shaped Mini—I have one in my office right now. Though you can only control it via Pura's app, scents last for over a month, and it does a great job at scenting a smaller space like a bedroom. My unit makes a high-pitched ringing noise, almost like an ultrasonic pest repellent, which is annoying, but Pura's customer service will likely replace yours if this happens to you.

There’s also the Pura Car, whose refills I will be purchasing during this sale (MSRP averages $21 apiece, and the four-week run time has been roughly accurate in my experience). Online reviews of this device are mixed, but I love mine. If you’re a parent, having Pura scents to inhale instead of old, spilled food and stinky soccer cleats is 100 percent worth the spend. Buy one for a mom you know, but only if she has USB charging ports in her car—it needs to be plugged in most of the time, as it doesn’t hold a charge for very long.

Also on sale for 20 percent off is Pura's fun upcoming Advent calendar, which features a Pura Home diffuser and 12 best-selling scents, most of which I have tried and can vouch for being options most people would enjoy.

Another Pura Cyber Week deal: Spend $50, and get 50 percent off the Pura Plus diffuser for large spaces, which has an MSRP of $80. I didn’t have the best of luck with the two Plus devices I went through—both eventually developed a loud buzzing noise. (Note that Pura will send you a replacement if this happens to you.) Additionally, unlike the Puras that sit flush to the outlet, this one is a cylinder that sits apart and must be plugged in at all times. It also makes an audible, fixed “shhhhhhh” noise as it’s long as it’s on (unlike the more intermittent noise emitted by competitors). However, it did do a great job of scenting a high-ceilinged room on the first floor of my house.

NASA’s Voyager 1 is now so far away that light takes 24 hours to reach it

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1655 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, NASA's Voyager 1 has achieved another extraordinary milestone, becoming the first spacecraft to reach a distance of one light-day from Earth.
  • According to recent reports, the historic moment occurred on November 18 at 2:16 a.m.
  • The achievement marks another remarkable chapter for a probe that has traveled farther than any other human-made object, survived decades beyond its original mission, and continues to explore a region of space that no spacecraft had previously entered.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, NASA's Voyager 1 has achieved another extraordinary milestone, becoming the first spacecraft to reach a distance of one light-day from Earth. After more than 49 years of traveling through space, humanity's most distant spacecraft is now approximately 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers) from home. At that distance, even a signal moving at the speed of light needs an entire day to make the journey.

According to recent reports, the historic moment occurred on November 18 at 2:16 a.m. PST (5:16 a.m. EST). Scientists and engineers at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, which is managed by Caltech, received a signal from Voyager 1 early Thursday, exactly 24 hours after the spacecraft reached the milestone.

The achievement marks another remarkable chapter for a probe that has traveled farther than any other human-made object, survived decades beyond its original mission, and continues to explore a region of space that no spacecraft had previously entered.

Voyager 1 Is Now 24 Light-Hours From Earth.

Sources indicate that astronomers often describe enormous cosmic distances in terms of how long light takes to travel them. A light-day represents the distance light covers in 24 hours, or roughly 16.1 billion miles.

Light moves through a vacuum at approximately 186,000 miles (299,000 kilometers) per second. To put Voyager 1's distance in perspective, sunlight passing Earth takes only about 1.3 seconds to reach the Moon. Reaching Neptune takes roughly four hours, while traveling from Neptune to Voyager 1 requires another 20 hours.

It has been revealed that even these enormous distances are small compared with those separating stars. A single light-year, the distance light travels in one year, measures approximately 5.88 trillion miles (9.46 trillion kilometers).

Voyager 1's extraordinary distance also creates a major challenge for mission controllers. Sending a command to the spacecraft now requires 24 hours, and receiving a response takes another 24 hours. A complete exchange therefore spans two full days, even though the signals travel at the fastest speed possible.

Recent findings suggest that the milestone comes as engineers investigate a communication problem. NASA has not received scientific or engineering data from Voyager 1 since November 14. However, the probe continues transmitting a carrier signal, the radio signal that normally carries information back to Earth. By tracking this signal and calculating the spacecraft's trajectory, mission specialists were able to verify that Voyager 1 had crossed the one light-day mark. Engineers are continuing to investigate why the expected data is not coming through.

A Historic Journey Beyond the Solar System's Planets.

Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, were launched in 1977 to take advantage of an unusual arrangement of the outer planets. The alignment allowed the spacecraft to use planetary gravity to travel from one destination to another, making an ambitious exploration mission possible.

Managed by JPL, the Voyagers became the third and fourth spacecraft to visit Jupiter and Saturn. They also delivered the first high-resolution images of these distant planets, revealing extraordinary fresh details about their atmospheres, rings, and moons. Voyager 2 continued farther, becoming the first spacecraft to explore Uranus and Neptune up close.

According to recent reports, today, both probes are traveling through interstellar space, making them humanity's only spacecraft to have crossed into the region beyond the Sun's protective bubble. Their instruments continue monitoring changes in the Sun's magnetic field across immense distances, providing scientists with measurements that cannot be collected from Earth.

"Traveling a light-day is a singular feat for a spacecraft, but Voyager is so much more than a distant traveler. The Voyager mission would be remarkable just for what it contributed to planetary science with the Grand Tour of the outer planets," said Joe Westlake, director, Heliophysics Division at NASA Headquarters in Washington. "But it went on to become central to NASA's fleet of heliophysics missions offering insights into the star that we all revolve around, the Sun.".

In a recent development, "Voyager 1 crossing the light-day threshold is yet another historic feat on an extraordinary voyage of discovery," remarked Dave Gallagher, JPL director. "Above all, this milestone stands as a testament to the exceptional teams who built, programmed, and fly these spacecraft today, and who have overcome countless challenges to keep them connected to Earth across the vastness of space. As NASA pushes toward newly introduced frontiers in human and robotic exploration, Voyager and the people behind its success continue to inspire us to reach farther and dream bigger.".

Voyager's Golden Record Carries a Message From Earth.

Sources indicate that the Voyager spacecraft carry more than scientific instruments. Each also holds a Golden Record, a gold-plated copper phonograph record containing images and sounds representing life on Earth. These recordings were designed as messages that an advanced extraterrestrial civilization might discover someday.

The records give the mission a purpose extending far beyond its scientific discoveries. Even after the spacecraft eventually lose the ability to communicate with Earth, they will continue traveling through space with a small collection of sights and sounds from the planet that launched them.

"Nearly half a century after leaving Earth, the Voyager mission continues to push the boundaries of human exploration. Its epic journey reflects the vision of Ed Stone, the Caltech physicist and JPL director who guided the mission for decades, and the curiosity and tenacity of generations of scientists and engineers who have carried that vision forward," stated Ray Jayawardhana, president, Caltech. "Beyond its immense contributions to science, Voyager also captures something profound about the human spirit. We may never know where its journey will ultimately lead, but it will venture on, an enduring affirmation that humanity was here and we yearned to explore.".

Exploring the Mysterious Region Beyond the Sun.

According to recent reports, voyager 1 is currently moving through space at approximately 38,000 mph (61,155 kph). In 2012, it became the first spacecraft to cross the boundary of the heliosphere, a vast region surrounding the Sun that is filled with particles and magnetic fields generated by our star.

Industry observers note that this protective bubble helps shield the solar system from cosmic radiation arriving from elsewhere in the galaxy. Beyond its outer boundary lies interstellar space, where particles and magnetic fields from the broader galaxy become more dominant.

Industry observers note that voyager 2 followed a different route and crossed into interstellar space in 2018. Together, the probes are providing the first direct observations of conditions beyond the heliosphere.

One of their most intriguing discoveries is that the Sun's effects do not simply disappear at the boundary. Its influence appears to extend much farther into interstellar space than scientists once understood, raising fresh questions about where the environment shaped by our star truly gives way to the surrounding galaxy.

Industry observers note that "The Voyagers are revolutionizing our understanding of interstellar space, a previously unexplored region outside the heliosphere," said Linda Spilker, Voyager project scientist at JPL. "One big surprise is the extent to which our Sun continues to affect interstellar space, all the way out to Voyager 1. Where does the Sun's influence end and pristine interstellar space begin? Perhaps Voyager may endure long enough to answer that question.".

How NASA Is Keeping Voyager 1 Alive After Nearly 50 Years.

Sources indicate that operating spacecraft built nearly half a century ago requires increasingly inventive engineering. Both Voyagers have experienced problems as their equipment ages, including clogged thrusters and a malfunctioning computer. NASA engineers have repeatedly developed solutions that allow the probes to continue working despite these setbacks.

Recent findings suggest that electricity has become one of the mission's greatest limitations. Earlier in 2026, engineers took a calculated risk by switching off three devices aboard Voyager 1 and replacing them with three alternatives that consume less power. This change was intended to help the spacecraft stretch its remaining energy supply.

According to recent reports, voyager 1 depends on a radioisotope thermal generator that is now approximately 50 years old. Often described as a nuclear battery, the device produces electricity by converting heat released during the radioactive decay of plutonium.

It has been revealed that as the radioactive material continues to decay, the available power gradually decreases. Both Voyager spacecraft lose approximately four watts of electrical output every year, forcing engineers to make difficult decisions about which systems can remain operational.

The latest conservation measures are expected to provide enough power to operate the spacecraft's current scientific instruments until at least the summer of 2027, when both probes will celebrate their 50th launch anniversaries.

One Day, Voyager 1 Will Become a Silent Messenger to the Stars.

Industry observers note that maintaining contact across such staggering distances requires some of NASA's most powerful communications equipment. The agency relies on its Deep Space Network, a worldwide system of large radio antennas located at three facilities, to communicate with Voyager and other spacecraft traveling to and beyond the Moon.

Sources indicate that despite the enormous communication delay and the spacecraft's aging systems, engineers continue monitoring Voyager 1 daily and transmitting instructions every week. The mission remains an extraordinary demonstration of what long-term spacecraft engineering can achieve.

"We listen to Voyager 1 every day and send commands to the spacecraft weekly. It just takes a little longer to communicate than it used to," said Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager at JPL. "Even traveling at the speed of light, signals now take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft and 24 hours to reach us. One day in the future, when it can no longer communicate with Earth, Voyager 1 will become humanity's silent ambassador to the stars.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European Union top officials and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham declared deals on trade and youth mobility at Friday's Brussels summit.

This might be the first step to rebuild ties, a decade after Britain voted to leave the EU.

During the delegations' meeting, Burnham said the deal was a "landmark agreement," while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called it a "turning point" in relations.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that "This is a good day for Britain. This is a good day for Europe," Burnham stated.

Speaking at the joint press conference, European Council President Antonio Costa said the bloc respected the British decision to leave the EU and would respect its choice to strengthen ties in the post-Brexit era.

He stated jokingly that the EU and UK "may drive on the opposite sides of the road, but what matters is they are heading for the same direction.".

Sources indicate that burnham said that the deals were made with young people in mind, adding: "This deal is for you. This deal really is about lifting your life chances.".

He went further and mentioned "Brexit took opportunities from young people," and that they have to "open up newly introduced opportunities" for young people.

Von der Leyen noted the youth experience project would "open horizons and create friendships that will last a lifetime.".

She said the trade agreement is a "two way street" and it means "more choice for the customers.".

Von der Leyen also mentioned the agreement on the carbon market, saying that it would cut emissions and generate investments in cleaner industries.

She also said Britain will rejoin the Erasmus+ program, adding, "We miss them so much.".

Burnham said the agreements reached Friday, however, represent the most the UK could achieve at the moment, "What we are announcing today is probably ‌the limit of what we can achieve in this ‌Parliament, given what needs ‌to be done to implement it.".

In September, Burnham said he would seek a political consensus on the country's future relationship with the EU, even suggesting he could campaign to take Britain back into the bloc at the next election.

According to recent reports, "Britain and Europe share values, interests and a global neighborhood. In a more dangerous world, we are stronger together. A closer partnership with Europe is good for working people, good for Britain and good for Europe," Burnham said as he arrived in Brussels.

The three key agreements establish ways to:.

The "youth experience scheme" would allow 100,000 people under 30 from each side to reside for up to three years in each other's territory for work, study or travel without being subject to existing visa requirements.

No deal was reached on tuition fees for EU students studying in Britain, a deal-breaker for the bloc. The EU has pressed for the UK to reduce university tuition fees for EU students to the same level paid by British students.

"There will be further discussions coming out of it on issues including on tuition fees," Burnham said.

Von der Leyen ‌noted ⁠she was confident negotiators would reach a ​solution ​on ‌tuition fees, "We will be working ‌on that in ‌the ​next month and as we have a ​track record of finding ⁠solutions,.".

In a recent development, on the food deal, the EU and UK have agreed to scrap certificates and border checks on food and animal products to ease post-Brexit trade. In return, Britain will align more closely with EU food safety and animal health rules.

They also agreed to link their emissions-trading systems, allowing them to recognize each other's carbon allowances and exempt traded goods from carbon border taxes.

According to the AFP news agency, London estimates the deal could boost the British economy by 3.8 billion pounds annually, and spare 6.5 billion pounds worth of steel, aluminum and other industrial exports from additional taxation.

Leaders said they will establish a "structured dialogue on migration." Their joint summit statement said this would include "engagement with third countries" and "returns to third countries," among other issues.

The two sides agreed to launch formal talks on economic security and strengthen cooperation on export controls and supply chains, among other areas.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Target on Wednesday reported its best sales growth in more than five years and beat Wall Street's revenue expectations, the latest signs of its turnaround strategy taking hold.

Industry observers note that the retailer said its net sales grew 7.1% during the fiscal third quarter. Comparable sales rose 5.6%, compared with StreetAccount estimates of up 3.8%. That growth was boosted by a 5% increase in comparable traffic, Target added.

"[It's] a healthy sign that guests are responding to our changes and choosing Target more often," CEO Michael Fiddelke told reporters.

Digital comparable sales jumped nearly 10% during the quarter.

Sources indicate that encouraged by the growth, Target raised its full-year guidance, upping its net sales growth guidance by 1 percentage point to around 6%. It's also expecting full-year operating income margin rate to be around 6.2%, which includes roughly 1.1 percentage points of benefit from tariff refunds.

The tech giant also noted it's now projecting full-year earnings per share to be in a range of $10.65 to $11.40, compared with prior guidance of between $9.90 and $10.90.

In a recent development, "The changes we've made across our assortment and guest experience are adding up," Fiddelke told reporters. "While we're encouraged by the progress, we know there's more work ahead to sustain this momentum and deliver consistent growth over time.".

Target shares climbed about 7% in afternoon trading Wednesday.

Here's how the company performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

Industry observers note that for the quarter ended Oct. 31, Target reported net income of $1.21 billion, or $2.65 per share, up from $689 million, or $1.51 per share, a year earlier.

This year, the company said it's invested approximately $3.8 billion in capital expenditures, up nearly $1 billion from last year. Because of those returns, Fiddelke said Target is now expecting to invest between $5 billion and $6 billion in capex next year.

On a call with analysts, he added that those investments will go toward more store remodels, technology, supply chain improvements, among other initiatives.

The company noted it saw particular strength in beauty, which saw 9% growth, and food and beverage, where sales increased nearly 7%. The retailer added that net sales rose in all three months of the third quarter, with the strongest performance during the back-to-school season.

Fiddelke told reporters the quarter's strength indicated "continued progress" toward Target's priorities that it outlined at the beginning of its turnaround.

As it looks to the holiday season, Target said it's marketing thousands of products priced at $5 and under, along with fresh artificial intelligence-powered shopping experiences to drive engagement. Fiddelke said Target is "encouraged" by shopping behaviors it's seen so far in the current quarter.

The big-box retailer has been showing signs of returning to growth, as it sees stronger sales trends after years of flat revenue. The results come after Target last quarter hiked its full fiscal-year outlook and remarked it saw "broad-based" strength across its various categories.

It has been revealed that it's also lowered prices on more than 10,000 items in an effort to get customers back into its stores, especially as consumer sentiment lags and inflation remains high. The retailer said on Wednesday that it cut prices on an additional roughly 2,000 items during the third quarter.

Target's stock is up more than 70% this year.

Breaking: Erdogan's political fate may be determined by Turkey's Kurds

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1508 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Turkey’s persecuted pro-Kurdish party has emerged as a kingmaker in the country’s upcoming election, playing a decisive role that may just tip the balance enough to unseat two-decade ruler Recep Tayyip Erdogan.
  • In a key setback to the Turkish president and leader of the Justice and Development Party (AK Party), the pro-Kurdish Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP) last month unveiled that it would not put forward its own presidential candidate, a move analysts say allows its supporters to vote for Erdogan’s main rival.
  • “We are facing a turning point that will shape the future of Turkey and (its) society,” noted the HDP in a statement on March 23.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Turkey’s persecuted pro-Kurdish party has emerged as a kingmaker in the country’s upcoming election, playing a decisive role that may just tip the balance enough to unseat two-decade ruler Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

In a key setback to the Turkish president and leader of the Justice and Development Party (AK Party), the pro-Kurdish Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP) last month unveiled that it would not put forward its own presidential candidate, a move analysts say allows its supporters to vote for Erdogan’s main rival.

“We are facing a turning point that will shape the future of Turkey and (its) society,” noted the HDP in a statement on March 23. “To fulfill our historical responsibility against the one-man rule, we will not field a presidential candidate in (the) May 14 elections.”.

It is a twist of irony for the Turkish strongman, who spent the better half of the past decade cracking down on the party after it began chipping away at his voter base. Its former leader Selahattin Demirtas has been in prison for nearly seven years and the party faces possible closure by a court for suspected collusion with the militant Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK) and affiliated groups. But its influence may nonetheless determine the course of Turkey’s politics.

The HDP’s decision not to field a candidate came just three days after head of the Republican People’s Party (CHP) Kemal Kilicdaroglu, Erdogan’s main rival, visited the party’s co-chairs. He told reporters that the solution to Turkey’s problems, “including the Kurdish problem” lies in parliament,” according to Turkish media.

Kilicdaroglu, who represents the six-party Nation Alliance opposition bloc, is the strongest contender to run against Erdogan in years. And while the HDP hasn’t yet unveiled whether it will put its weight behind him, analysts say it is the kingmaker in the elections.

Erdogan's 'polar opposite' wants to replace him as president of Turkey.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a carefully crafted political discourse,” Hisyar Ozsoy, deputy co-chair of the HDP and a member of parliament from the predominantly Kurdish province of Diyarbakir, told CNN. “We are not going to have our own candidate, and we will leave it to the international community to interpret it the way they wish.”.

Experts say the crackdown on the HDP is rooted in the threat it poses to Erdogan politically, as well as its position as one of the main parties representing Turkey’s Kurds, an ethnic minority from which a separatist militant movement has emerged.

In a recent development, the party and the Kurdish people have had a complicated relationship with Erdogan. The leader courted the Kurds in earlier years by granting them more rights and reversing restrictions on the use of their language. Relations with the HDP were also cordial once, as Erdogan worked with the party on a brief peace process with the PKK.

But ties between Erdogan and the HDP later turned sour, and the HDP fell under a sweeping crackdown aimed at the PKK and their affiliates.

Kurds are the biggest minority in Turkey, making up between 15% and 20% of the population, according to Minority Rights Group International.

It is unclear if the HDP will endorse Kilicdaroglu, but analysts say that the deliberate distance may be beneficial for the opposition candidate.

According to recent reports, the accusations against the HDP place it in a precarious position during the elections. It presently faces a case in Turkey’s Constitutional Court over suspected ties to the PKK, which is designated as a terrorist group by Turkey, the United States and the European Union. Knowing it may be banned at any moment, its candidates are running under the Green Left Party in parliament.

If the opposition is seen as allying with the HDP, Erdogan’s AK Party may use its influence in the media to discredit it as being pro-PKK, mentioned Murat Somer, a political science professor at Koc University in Istanbul and author of Return to Point Zero, a book on the Turkish-Kurdish question in Turkey.

According to recent reports, the HDP’s threat to Erdogan’s hold on power became apparent after the June 2015 election, the first general election it participated in. It won 13% of the seats, denying the ruling AK Party its majority for the first time since 2002. Erdogan, however, called a snap election five months later, which led to a drop in the HDP’s support to 10.7%, as well as the restoration of the AK Party’s overall majority.

According to recent reports, “They are a kingmaker in these elections because the HDP gets about half of the votes of the Kurdish population in Turkey,” remarked Somer, adding that the other, more conservative Kurdish voters have traditionally voted for Erdogan’s AK Party. And last month, the Free Cause Party (HUDA-PAR), a tiny Kurdish-Islamist party revealed support for Erdogan in the elections. The party has never won seats in parliament.

Erdogan's political fate may rest on his response to the earthquake.

The HDP knows that its position is key to the outcome of next month’s vote, but that it’s also in a delicate situation.

“We want to play the game wisely, and we need to be very careful,” said Ozsoy, adding that the party wants to avoid a “contaminated political climate” where the elections are polarized “between a very ugly ultra-nationalist discourse against Kilicdaroglu and others.”.

The party was founded in 2012 with a number of aims, said Ozsoy, one of which was “peaceful and democratic resolution of the Kurdish conflict.”.

Somer noted that the party was seen to be “an initiative” of the PKK, which later led to a heavy government crackdown on it in the name of counterterrorism.

Its former leader Demirtas remains an influential figure.

The Turkish government has been trying to link the HDP to the PKK but has so far failed to prove “a real connection,” stated Asli Aydintasbas, a visiting fellow at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC.

Recent findings suggest that A post-Erdogan Turkey may give some breathing space to the Kurds and Kurdish-dominated parties in Turkey, Aydintasbas told CNN, noting that many Kurdish voters have recently left Erdogan’s camp. “For HDP, this is more than just an ideological choice,” she mentioned. “It’s a matter of survival.”.

Ozsoy says his party understands what’s at stake, not only for Turkey’s Kurds but for all its minorities.

It has been revealed that “We are aware of our responsibility here. We are aware of our role. We know we are in a kingmaker position,” the HDP lawmaker stated.

Two women arrested for not wearing hijab following ‘yogurt attack’.

Two women were arrested in Iran for failing to wear the hijab in public, after a man threw a tub of yogurt at them at a store in the city of Shandiz on Thursday, according to Mizan News Agency, the state-run outlet for Iran’s judiciary.

Oil prices surge after OPEC+ producers announce surprise cuts.

Recent findings suggest that oil prices spiked Monday after OPEC+ producers unexpectedly declared that they would cut output. Brent crude, the global benchmark, jumped 5.31% to $84.13 a barrel, while WTI, the US benchmark, rose 5.48% to $79.83. Both were the sharpest price rises in almost a year. The collective output cut by the nine members of OPEC+ totals 1.66 million barrels per day.

Iran blames Israel for the killing of second IRGC officer, vows to respond.

A second Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) officer died following an attack in Syria on Friday, according to Iranian state media on Sunday. Iranian state media mentioned the Iranian military adviser died after an Israeli attack near the Syrian capital Damascus left him wounded. The attack also killed another IRGC officer. In a tweet on Sunday, Iranian government spokesman Ali Bahadori Jahromi said the alleged Israeli attack wouldn’t go unanswered. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Nasser Kanaani said on Sunday that Iran has the right to respond to “state terrorism.”.

Iranian-American comedian Maz Jobrani, who has been touring the Middle East, spoke to CNN’s Becky Anderson about his support for the protests in his homeland, saying that he used his standup comedy platform to highlight the “brutality against the Iranian people.”.

“It was an opportunity for me to say, ‘let’s keep fighting,’” he remarked.

An Iranian state news outlet is gloating at what it sees as the demise of the US dollar.

IRNA recreated a popular meme to mark China and Brazil’s decision to reportedly ditch the US dollar as an intermediary in trade, citing the Chinese state news outlet, China Daily. It demonstrates two men representing China and Brazil posing in front of a grave labelled “USD.”.

Sources indicate that the meme was pinned to the top of IRNA’s Twitter page, and was met with laughter and ridicule. “Dream on,” mentioned another user, pointing to the dollar’s use as the main reserve currency around the world.

China Daily remarked that the agreement was part of “the rising global use of the Chinese renminbi.” It would reportedly enable China and Brazil to conduct trade and financial transactions using local currencies instead of the dollar.

Tech Report: Republican senator blocks Trump cyber nominee over January 6 denial

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thom Tillis move comes after Michael LoSapio, nominated for Cisa role, told hearing ‘I don’t believe it was an attack’.
  • Senator Thom Tillis, the outgoing North Carolina Republican who is due to be replaced by a Democrat, has reportedly blocked a confirmation vote on Donald Trump’s nominee to lead a key US cybersecurity agency, Michael LoSapio, after he denied during a hearing that the Capitol was attacked on January 6 2021.
  • In a recent development, tillis, who declined to run for re-election and after repeated clashes with Trump’s, confirmed to HuffPost on Friday that he has placed a hold on LoSapio’s nomination to serve as a director of the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Agency (Cisa).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thom Tillis move comes after Michael LoSapio, nominated for Cisa role, told hearing ‘I don’t believe it was an attack’.

Senator Thom Tillis, the outgoing North Carolina Republican who is due to be replaced by a Democrat, has reportedly blocked a confirmation vote on Donald Trump’s nominee to lead a key US cybersecurity agency, Michael LoSapio, after he denied during a hearing that the Capitol was attacked on January 6 2021.

In a recent development, tillis, who declined to run for re-election and after repeated clashes with Trump’s, confirmed to HuffPost on Friday that he has placed a hold on LoSapio’s nomination to serve as a director of the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Agency (Cisa). His block on the nomination will prevent it from being included in a package of nominees to be voted on next month, before the Republicans lose their majority in the Senate.

At his Senate confirmation hearing on Thursday, LoSapio, the chief information security officer for Palantir, a technology firm founded by JD Vance’s mentor, Peter Thiel, was asked by senator Richard Blumenthal, a Connecticut Democrat: “Was there an attack on the Capitol of January 6 2021?”.

After initially replying, “I don’t know,” LoSapio said: “No, I don’t believe it was an attack.”.

Tillis told the Hill that the question of whether a mob of Trump supporters attacked the US Capitol in an attempt to overturn Joe Biden’s 2020 victory was not open for debate.

Sources indicate that “It’s binary,” Tillis told the outlet. “The minute you pretend like it didn’t exist or you can’t even acknowledge it, I don’t have any time because it’s not a very thoughtful person.”.

The agency LoSapio was nominated by Trump to lead, Cisa, plays a role in protecting US elections infrastructure from hacking.

The week after the 2020 election, as Trump falsely claimed that count had been rigged, Cisa was one of a number of federal agencies with oversight of election infrastructure to issue a statement calling the election “the most secure in American history” and noting that there was “no evidence that any voting system deleted or lost votes, changed votes, or was in any way compromised.”.

After he returned to the White House last year, Trump signed an April 2025 presidential memorandum directing executive offices to take steps to address supposed “risks from Chris Krebs”, who led Cisa in 2020.

“Krebs, through CISA, falsely and baselessly denied that the 2020 election was rigged and stolen, including by inappropriately and categorically dismissing widespread election malfeasance and serious vulnerabilities with voting machines,” Trump’s memorandum claimed.

If you are trying to get your hands on a PlayStation 5 right now, the real win is not a discount — it is simply finding one in stock at standard retail price. Between a global RAM shortage driven by the AI boom, which pushed Sony to hike console prices twice in under a year, and the massive hype around GTA 6, standalone console markdowns are nowhere to be found.

Sources indicate that today, the PS5 Slim Digital Edition starts at $599.99, and the flagship PS5 Pro retails for $899.99. Depending on the model, that means PlayStation 5 hardware actually costs $150 to $200 more today than it did when the console originally released in 2020.

In a recent development, for weeks, the hype around GTA 6 completely wiped out store shelves across the country — especially for the PS5 Pro. The good news is that major retailers like Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Amazon are finally restocking standard PS5 models at regular list price.

We recommend paying full sticker price, because third-party marketplace listings are barely worth looking at anyway — the few that are up are mostly refurbished units marked up to nearly double the retail cost, so we left them off our list.

Even at full sticker price, picking up a PS5 or PS5 Pro makes a lot of sense if you are upgrading for GTA 6 or catching up on Sony's massive library of current-gen games.

The standard PlayStation 5 Digital Edition gives you the core current-gen experience in a slim, compact design that fits easily into a media console. You get an 825GB ultra-high-speed SSD that cuts load screens to seconds, 4K TV output, up to 120 fps gameplay on supported titles, and Tempest 3D AudioTech. Recent findings suggest that it also ships with Sony's DualSense wireless controller — featuring haptic feedback and adaptive triggers that add physical resistance when you pull a trigger or drive over rough terrain — and plays more than 8,500 backward-compatible PS4 games with smoother frame rates. Plus, if you ever decide you want to buy physical discs later, you can snap Sony's detachable disc drive right onto the side.

If you want the best possible visuals in Vice City, stepping up to the PlayStation 5 Pro unlocks PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) for sharper AI-upscaled clarity, upgraded GPU performance, and advanced ray tracing. While Rockstar confirmed GTA 6 targets 30 fps across all consoles at launch, the PS5 Pro is the only system that gets exclusive ray-traced shadows and cleaner image upscaling in the game.

Beyond GTA 6, dozens of major PS5 titles run at higher frame rates and sharper resolutions on the Pro, and its massive 2TB SSD easily swallows GTA 6's 212GB install size with plenty of storage left over for the rest of your library.

It is the most reliable way to shave real money off the console without gambling on sketchy third-party resellers.

Recent findings suggest that you might also spot occasional game bundles at big-box stores, though availability is hit-or-miss. Even the overpriced bundles and double-the-price third-party listings floating around online are largely sold out, proving just how intense the demand still is.

After watching store shelves sit completely empty less than a week ago, seeing major retailers finally restock both the PS5 and PS5 Pro is a welcome surprise. If you are trying to jump into GTA 6 without paying double to a reseller, grab an official unit at retail price — or check PlayStation Direct's refurbished store — before this wave clears out too.

  • Early in Shakespeare’s tragedy Julius Caesar, the title character is publicly offered a crown as a symbol of absolute power.
  • He did not even wait until a crown was offered before grabbing for it.
  • Huang, used to exercising power, seemed as energized as the mob supporting Caesar had been.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Early in Shakespeare’s tragedy Julius Caesar, the title character is publicly offered a crown as a symbol of absolute power. Caesar refuses it three times, dramatically fainting after the final try. Scholars say that Caesar’s “falling sickness,” as his eventual assassin Brutus put it, masked his true intention to rule. His effort to win over the crowd with his humility only intensified the momentum to grant him more power. Indeed, after his refusal, his adherents became even more impassioned, setting the stage for his eventual claim to kingship. “If Caesar had stabb’d their mothers, they would have done no less,” said a Roman senator of the sycophantic crowd.

Jensen Huang was not so strategic. He did not even wait until a crown was offered before grabbing for it. On November 12, Nvidia’s cofounder had resigned from his post as CEO, promising to work to heal his family and earn back trust. The reasons were obvious. He had been engaging in an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Under his leadership, billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia’s sales had gone to her formerly obscure tech giant in Singapore, which, in a potential violation of export regulations, the company used to power Chinese AI efforts. In addition, he was carrying on an affair with an Nvidia subordinate (or was it two?), itself a fireable transgression. Nonetheless, because of his success in building Nvidia, Huang has been receiving a noisy groundswell of support from Silicon Valley and Wall Street, with the same loyalty as the crowd that would have idolized Caesar even if he’d stabbed their mothers.

Huang, used to exercising power, seemed as energized as the mob supporting Caesar had been. Social media was exploding with memes portraying him as a hero whose return would result in Homeric redemption. Silicon Valley leaders like Travis Kalanick, Tim Sweeney, and Elon Musk called his removal an injustice that must be addressed. One of Huang’s talents is moving fast. So perhaps he used state-of-the-art Rubin GPUs to dispatch an armada of AI introspection-bots, fast-tracking what formerly would have taken months of moral cleansing into a few days. In any case, on November 17, when the pixels on his resignation message had barely settled, he returned to X to announce that he would be honored to reclaim his position if offered.

In a recent development, it was not to be. Within hours, Nvidia’s board threw more water on Huang’s overture than a Texas data center consumes in a year. During a scheduled earnings call, chair Harvey Jones mentioned, “The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation but does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO.” Nvidia’s interim leader, Colette Kress, who had been its long-time CFO, ended the call with a devastating kicker: “We’ve got this.” Et tu, Colette?

Industry observers note that the search for a replacement will proceed. But even after the board presumably closed the door, and Kress told employees in an all-hands meeting once again that “we got this,” the push to restore him has not quieted. The president of the United States hasn’t retracted his opinion that Huang should resume his post. A petition called “Stand With Jensen” now has over 200,000 signatures. Hedge funder Bill Ackman zinged out a hysterical X post this week charging “major governance failures by directors.” (Clearly, Ackman’s view of ideal governance is no governance.) Most alarmingly, Semafor has reported that Huang himself had spoken to at least one board member about his reinstatement and that several directors may still be open to the possibility. At press time, Huang has not given any public indication that he is no longer angling for a triumphant return.

Industry observers note that at the Upcoming York Times DealBook conference, held a day after the earnings call, the Jensen affair dominated the discussion, even as Anthropic was readying the biggest IPO in history. On stage, OpenAI’s Sam Altman and Greg Brockman expressed admiration for Huang but did not recommend his reinstatement. But Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey remarked that “nobody can take Jensen’s place in this critical juncture” because “his personal relations are the reason everyone is willing to do business” with Nvidia. Elon Musk reaffirmed his outrage that Huang had been forced out, saying it was like the Chicago Bulls firing Michael Jordan in his prime during a playoff hot streak. In my informal conversations during breaks, I found people on both sides of the divide. One person was a substantial Nvidia investor who showed me pictures of themselves with Huang. Like many with a financial stake in the organization, this individual was eager to see Huang back in charge.

It has been revealed that everyone is in agreement that the Huang story is tragic. But the outcry for Huang’s reinstatement is a broader tragedy, revealing how greed has eclipsed ethics and patriotism. Those clamoring for reinstatement have one argument: that Huang’s leadership was so singular and superlative that he must keep his job. Not doing so would dishonor his previous efforts and degrade Nvidia’s future performance. Essentially, it’s an ends-justify-the-means rationale incompatible with corporate oversight and even fidelity to law and national security.

The push to reinstate Huang is also a grotesque extension of the cult of the founder, which assumes that those who built a tech giant have unique abilities to run it and should be unconstrained in how they do so. (Serious question: If founders are so great, why do the vast majority of startups fail?).

There’s no question that Huang has built one of the greatest companies ever and delivered historic returns to shareholders. But one irony of the Bring Back Jensen Movement is that this crisis has exposed him, in some respects, as an erratic, even a lousy, CEO. His personal indiscretions cost shareholders almost a trillion dollars! He lied to his board. He pursued a strategy that seems to have violated the spirit if not the law of export regulations. He gave senior executive posts to family members who pursued a passion in the chip business later in life, including his daughter (trained as a chef), son (went to art school and owned a cocktail lounge), and son-in-law (former professional skier). In a public manufacturer, nepotism comes at shareholders’ expense.

On top of that, he failed in a critical duty of a CEO—preparing a succession initiative. Nvidia has none, solely because Huang acted as if he would run it forever. At DealBook, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, after the obligatory expressions of empathy toward Huang, threw some shade on leaders who don’t plan for their departure: “People get old and die,” he mentioned. “If a company will succeed, it needs someone to take over. I’ve never trusted a leader, founder or otherwise, who states the institution after I left was completely gone. Like, then what did you build?”.

Industry observers note that finally, if Huang were so passionate about Nvidia’s future, why is he still angling for a return? The possibility, even a remote one, that he will be reinstated may discourage the best candidates from considering an offer to lead Nvidia. Huang would best serve Nvidia by shutting down the talk from his Silicon Valley cronies and demanding that the Bring Jensen Back petition be scrapped.

It has been revealed that ultimately, by giving up his quest to reclaim the crown, Huang would better serve not only Nvidia but himself. His energy should be devoted first to mending his family relations and then working with lawyers to maintain his reputation, fortune, and maybe even freedom. There’s an additional bonus to his departure. He will be leaving Nvidia at a peak for high-powered GPU chips and AI’s economic power. If the bubble does pop, Huang will avoid being the face of AI when the fall comes. Remember, things didn’t work out too well for Julius Caesar.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Hundreds of people came out to honor and celebrate the life and legacy of the California civil rights activist Dolores Huerta at a celebration-of-life event Friday in Bakersfield.
  • Huerta’s daughter Lori de Leon thanked attendees for their support during her mother’s passing, highlighting the widespread tributes and communities gathering in her honor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A public vigil and celebration of life honor the civil rights activist and co-founder of United Farm Workers union.

Hundreds of people came out to honor and celebrate the life and legacy of the California civil rights activist Dolores Huerta at a celebration-of-life event Friday in Bakersfield.

Huerta’s daughter Lori de Leon thanked attendees for their support during her mother’s passing, highlighting the widespread tributes and communities gathering in her honor.

Huerta’s casket was escorted inside the Dignity Health arena for the interfaith memorial service as Mariachi Lindas Mexicanas played next to it.

Huerta, a feminist icon who co-founded the United Farm Workers (UFW) in 1962, died on 28 October aged 96.

Sources indicate that attenders came from all over California to pay their respects. Rosa de la Cruz, a 44-year-old farm worker who lives in Tulare, about an hour north of Bakersfield, stated she wanted to pay her respects in person.

The world-renowned labor rights leader and activist means “a great deal”, de la Cruz remarked, “because if it hadn’t been for her, there wouldn’t be many benefits for the people who work in the fields.”.

The week was filled with events dedicated to Huerta’s memory, her courage, resilience and her impact on the community.

On Monday, Huerta was honored in Sacramento by state government officials including Monique Limón, the senate president pro tempore, Robert Rivas, the assembly speaker, Xavier Becerra, the California governor-elect, and community leaders in a historic ceremony.

It has been revealed that huerta became the first female, first Latino and first non-elected leader to lie in honor at the state capitol. Her casket was escorted in after a march organized by local unions.

“Our mother devoted her entire life to fighting injustice and lifting up communities too often left out and treated unfairly,” said Huerta’s family. “As a lifelong organizer, her activism has been a source of inspiration and empowerment for people around the world.”.

For more than six decades, Huerta spearheaded historic boycotts, fought tirelessly for farm workers’ rights, women’s equality and environmental justice, and coined the enduring national rally cry, “¡Sí, se puede!”.

According to recent reports, huerta has received numerous honors including the Eleanor Roosevelt Human Rights Awards. In 2012, Barack Obama awarded Huerta the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation’s highest civilian honor.

The two-day tribute started on Thursday evening with a public rosary and vigil in Bakersfield, where she had lived since 1990.

Sources indicate that friday’s interfaith memorial service and celebration of life began with an opening blessing by Aztec dancers. There were performances from music groups Los Lobos, Ozomatli, Las Cafeteras, Nancy Sanchez and Trio los Dados. Rob Bonta, the California attorney general, was among the speakers on Friday.

“Dolores Huerta is irreplaceable and her loss is something I think people are still, including me, getting our heads around,” Bonta said. “To the world, she is an icon and a giant and a legend. For me, she was also a friend and a mentor and a counselor. Someone I texted with and called and sought advice from and leaned on as I launched my career and had my career in elected public office.”.

According to recent reports, “Her loss is immeasurable. She is irreplaceable but she leaves a legacy of fighting for justice,” Bonta noted.

According to recent reports, ten of Huerta’s adult children took the stage to share personal anecdotes about Huerta’s life, emphasizing her skills as an organizer, political strategist and motivational speaker. Her children recounted her dedication to social justice, her love for jazz, and her humility despite her significant contributions.

Sources indicate that “While there is much to celebrate in our recent victories, there is still so much work to be done,” said Huerta’s daughter Camila Chavez. “People may expect us to fill her shoes, but she is going to be buried with her shoes. Like Zapata said: ‘I’d rather live on my feet than die on my knees.’ It’s going to take all of us here to fill those shoes.”.

It has been revealed that her legacy will continue through the work and empowering mission of the Dolores Huerta Foundation. In 2003, Huerta founded the grassroots community organization to create leadership opportunities for community members, while organizing underserved communities, and pursuing social justice.

Huerta kept on working even as a nonagenarian, dedicating her life as an organizer.

In a recent development, in the Central valley, Huerta supported minorities to run for office to make a difference at the local, state and federal level. In a 2022 speech, Huerta encouraged newly introduced US citizens to fulfill their civic responsibilities, especially voting.

For her 94th birthday, Huerta asked people to help her celebrate by getting others involved in elections either by talking to somebody about voting and about registering to vote.

Huerta urged uninsured Latinos and Californians to enroll in health coverage with the passage of the Affordable Care Act partnering with Covered California to spread the message. Huerta also had several schools named after her throughout the state. Last year, Huerta joined Central valley educators to demand David Valadao, a US representative from California, defend funding for schools.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • They are veterans – many, like Golov, from elite forces – who now feel they are fighting on a newly introduced battlefield: To save Israeli democracy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a sea of Israeli flags, Yiftach Golov holds one that looks a little different.

Among the hundreds of thousands of protesters who took to the streets for the 13th week in a row on Saturday, Golov hoists a brown flag that represents a group called “Brother and Sisters in Arms.”.

They are veterans – many, like Golov, from elite forces – who now feel they are fighting on a newly introduced battlefield: To save Israeli democracy.

“We believe this is our responsibility to go once again called to the flag of the nation to stop this madness to defend Israel,” Golov said, as he weaved his way through the protesters on Tel Aviv’s Kaplan street, between the high-rises that house many of Israel’s high tech companies.

Sources indicate that during the second intifada, in the early 2000s, Golov served in a special forces reconnaissance unit. He was never before particularly political, focusing more on getting his PhD in biophysics from Tel Aviv University.

But when the protest movement against the Israeli government’s judicial overhaul plan began in January, Golov attended one a demonstration and soon became one of thousands of veterans, and now military reservists, who have taken up the cause as their new mission.

Some, including elite Air Force reservists, have taken it a step further, threatening not to heed the call to train or even serve in protest of the government’s aims planned judicial changes, which would give the governing parties more control over Israel’s judiciary.

Industry observers note that others have taken to becoming some of the most active organizers and demonstrators. Last week, a group from Brothers and Sisters in Arms protested by carrying a figure wrapped in the Israeli flag on a stretcher, the way they would carry a wounded comrade off the field.

While Golov indicates he has not taken the drastic step to refuse service, he understands the motivation.

“We’re fighting for justice and liberty, just like the American story, that’s the values that that are being represented symbolized back when we look at our flag, that’s something that was lacking lacking for the last few decades. So basically, we reclaim the flag,” he said.

Palestinian taxi driver recounts surviving attack by right-wing protesters.

Recent findings suggest that fellow members of the group, all wearing brown shirts with the organization’s logo, come up and say hello. They’re sprinkled all throughout the protests. One is even leading the “Pink Front,” a group of coordinated drummers who look like they are dressed for a rave, and often lead the chants at the protests.

They’re using skills they learned in the military – how to organize, how to mobilize – now for the protests. But more importantly, they say they have the same type of motivation.

Sources indicate that “The very deep feeling that you are part of something bigger than yourself, that (you’re) allowed to sacrifice anything that is needed, whether it’s your career, health, seriously mental health,” Golov mentioned. “We all have a mission, you’re willing to do it at any cost. You’re very determined, you know that you are on the right side, you’re carrying the torch of light. That keeps us being highly motivated despite the fact that we’re not sleeping for days.”.

Israel’s protest movement is made up of many disparate groups, but the pressure from Israel’s much vaunted veterans has been seen as a key to moving the needle.

Last Monday, after weeks of sustained protests and the largest general strike in Israeli history, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced a pause to the legislation, to allow time for negotiations with the opposition.

According to recent reports, but despite the announcements, protesters are still out in the streets in large numbers. CNN affiliate Channel 12 in Israel estimated the size of Saturday’s demonstration in Tel Aviv at about 150,000 people. Organizers claimed it was 230,000.

Last week’s mass protests and widespread strike action came after Netanyahu remarked he had decided to fire Defense Minister Yoav Gallant for advocating a delay in passing the legislation – a move that Netanyahu has since delayed, sources told CNN, due to “the present security situation.”.

Sources indicate that in his televised speech calling for a delay, Gallant had mentioned the pause in the legislation was needed “for the security of Israel,” citing the refusal of some Israel Defense Forces reservists to train in protest of the government plans. He said pressing ahead with the proposals could threaten Israel’s security.

Under pressure at home and from allies abroad, Netanyahu said he would delay votes on the remaining legislation until after the Knesset’s Passover recess in April “to give time for a real chance for a real debate.”.

“Out of the responsibility to the nation, I decided to delay … the vote, in order to give time for discussion,” he added.

According to recent reports, but Netanyahu indicated that the delay was only temporary. He insisted that the overhaul was necessary, and reiterated criticism of refusal to train or serve in the military in protest at the planned changes. “Refusing is the end of our country,” he stated.

Many protesters don’t believe that the pause is real, or say it’s simply a stalling tactic to give Netanyahu some breathing room and get the protesters to go home before he plows on with the reforms.

“We will start doing deactivation only when we will know 100% that Israel state will stay a functional democratic country. Whatever needs to be done for that,” Golov mentioned.
