Traumatized teens sue school, cops after Doritos bag triggers AI gun alert

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1711 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In October 2025, four Black high school students were sharing Cool Ranch Doritos after football practice, winding down and waiting for their rides home.
  • Recent findings suggest that within two minutes, Baltimore County Public Schools officials who reviewed security camera footage linked to the alert determined there was no actual threat.
  • The false alert could have ended there—before a traumatizing campus clash with police—but it didn’t.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In October 2025, four Black high school students were sharing Cool Ranch Doritos after football practice, winding down and waiting for their rides home. It was then, in the lull of a moment any teen with after-school activities knows well, that the school’s AI gun detection system suddenly flagged one teen holding a bag of chips as a potential gunman.

Recent findings suggest that within two minutes, Baltimore County Public Schools officials who reviewed security camera footage linked to the alert determined there was no actual threat. They recognized the Doritos bag and canceled the alert, which notified not only other school officials but also the Baltimore County Police Department that no response was needed.

The false alert could have ended there—before a traumatizing campus clash with police—but it didn’t.

According to a lawsuit filed by the current and former students, Taki Allen, Yui-Osa Ogbeide, Devon Thompson Jr., and Keith Winfield III, due to “both technological and human errors,” school officials called police to the scene anyway, and the cops responded with force.

It has been revealed that at least six patrol cars arrived with lights flashing, and some cops emerged with guns drawn. The teens froze and cooperated, confused and scared for their lives, their lawsuit noted.

It has been revealed that “No one told the students what they were suspected of,” the lawsuit said. “Officers separated the students, ordered them to their knees on the concrete, handcuffed them, and searched their persons and property.”.

Only after the cops failed to find a gun did students learn that it was the school’s AI gun detection system, Omnilert, that triggered the police response. Allegedly, one of the responding officers muttered, “stupid AI cameras” and “fucking Omnilerts,” while another told the students that “AI is not the best.” Finally releasing the students, one officer seemed to acknowledge that they had put the teens in danger.

“Hey, thanks for not running away, that would have been a real problem,” the officer allegedly stated. Walking away, another joked that the boys should remember to “be careful with your chip bags.”.

The cops did not just target the suspected gunman but apparently told the other teens that they were guilty “by association” when they asked why they were searched.

Suing to stop any other teens from facing allegedly life-or-death situations due to officials’ blind trust of AI, the teens have asked for an injunction barring BCPS from using Omnilert until they can effectively establish protocols to prevent police responses to false alerts.

The lawsuit alleged that students’ constitutional rights were violated, as students were unlawfully searched and detained.

Damon Hewitt, president and executive director of the Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights Under Law—a nonpartisan nonprofit that’s representing the teens in the suit—noted that “overreliance on artificial intelligence technology mixed with inept communication and coordination among key officials is a toxic mix.”.

Industry observers note that the complaint noted that BCPS was among the earliest adopters of Omnilert, and officials have touted it as “the largest deployment of AI visual gun detection” as a means to supposedly protect students. Instead, they alleged that Omnilert is marketing a defective product as triggering “near-zero false positives” without effectively requiring the adequate human review that claim depends on.

“We need a reckoning on how AI is being used, especially concerning public safety and kids,” Hewitt noted. “We are fighting to deliver justice in this case, but it also holds lessons for educators and police officials across the country who should think twice before putting our children’s fate in the hands of AI.”.

It has been revealed that all the teens feel less safe on campus and less trusting of police following the incident. They also suffered from physical pain—including ”deep red marks” on their wrists from handcuffs—as well as “acute and lasting emotional distress, fear, anxiety,” and “humiliation.” Further, the teens report that rumors follow them around, falsely claiming that there was a gun and damaging their reputations.

It has been revealed that car pick-up will never be the same. The student falsely flagged as the gunman, Taki Allen, “no longer feels safe waiting for rides or spending time outside the school after hours” and “frequently pays for rides home from private car services to avoid waiting for rides from friends or family.” Keith Winfield’s house was very close to the school, but his mother, Frieda Winfield, said his anxiety was so bad that he would call her “multiple times after football practice ended to confirm that she was on her way to pick him up.”.

Frieda Winfield called for change following her son Keith’s chilling interaction.

According to recent reports, “The police told my son this could have been a real problem,” Frieda Winfield said. “No child in Baltimore County should face this kind of danger while waiting outside his own school for a ride home from his mother.”.

It has been revealed that the teens’ lawsuit targets Omnilert and responding Baltimore County Police Department officers. It also challenges Baltimore County Public Schools and individual school officials who allegedly failed to establish proper protocols to prevent a police response to a canceled alert.

In a later investigation, the Office of the Inspector General (OIG) for Education concluded that Omnilert’s system had no “bias.” But OIG acknowledged that the “delegation of authority” process that Kenwood High School set up didn’t stop its principal, Kate Smith, from noticing the alert, failing to see it was canceled, and texting a school resource officer to deploy police 15 minutes later—all while acknowledging in that text that the object in the alert was “maybe not” a gun. Smith apparently was never trained on the Omnilert system, OIG’s report indicated.

The OIG agreed with teens that things should change. Immediately after the incident, an internal Omnilert training link was shared with BCPS staff, and OIG recommended that schools conduct biannual trainings moving forward.

They also recommended that the BCPS Department of School Safety “review its protocol” and reduce the number of individuals who receive campus gun alerts. That could help ensure “internal notification controls are followed” and police “are fully informed of a verified threat,” the OIG said.

Without changes, the OIG acknowledged that “the loss of alert notification controls could place not only BCPS staff and students at risk but could also place responding law enforcement in a potentially tragic situation.”.

According to recent reports, another change offered a technical solution that may have prevented the tragic event. The OIG recommended that school officials switch to using the Omnilert app. Since Smith opened the alert in a text message window on her phone, they suggested that she could easily have overlooked the cancellation text message if her first instinct were to enlarge the image or review the camera footage.

According to recent reports, these recommendations aren’t enough for current and former students suing, one of whom remains an active student who claims the principal never apologized and instead made light of the incidents using cry-laughing emojis in texts with other school officials. Teens alleged that Smith should have known that more than “99 percent of OGD Alerts in Baltimore County Public Schools were false positives that required no police response,” as the OIG’s report said, and she should have prioritized students’ safety and verified the threat before calling in police.

“BCPS’s failures amounted to deliberate indifference to the constitutional rights of its students,” their lawsuit alleged.

The teens asked a court for an injunction barring the use of Omnilert until BCPS staff and police are adequately trained. In their complaint, they alleged that none of the officers on the scene had reviewed the camera footage before responding, and none of the officers informed of the alert cancellation intervened.

According to recent reports, BCPS declined to comment on the lawsuit, pointing Ars to a statement issued to parents following the incident. That statement did not directly apologize to students but did say the school would provide “ongoing counseling and emotional support” to them while promising to take steps to prevent future incidents.

Blake Mitchell, Omnilert’s vice president of marketing, told Ars that Omnilert is reviewing the complaint.

“What these four students went through on October 20, 2025 should not have happened, and we are truly sorry for the fear they and their families experienced,” Mitchell remarked. “We understand why they want answers.”.

Mitchell mentioned that Omnilert is “built to send anything that could be a firearm to trained people for review, because missing a real gun is the worst possible outcome.” He also reiterated that the OIG investigation found no bias in Omnilert’s system and seemed to agree that it was the school’s authority delegation that failed the students, not necessarily the technology.

“In this case, the school’s designated safety staff reviewed the alert and canceled it within about two minutes, and everyone who received it was notified,” Mitchell said. “That is exactly why human review matters, and why a canceled alert must stay canceled.”.

Len Kamdang of the Lawyers’ Committee representing the teens told The New York Times that teens want BCPS and Omnilert to acknowledge that “what happened to them was unacceptable.”.

“This case is ultimately about how human beings allowed AI to substitute for their judgment,” Kamdang noted.

As a mother, Frieda Winfield told a local news outlet that she was shocked by the incident, despite deliberately teaching her son to be cautious around police. The boys’ caution “saved their lives in my opinion,” she said.

Industry observers note that “I was angry. I was fearful,” Frieda Winfield said. “The biggest part was fear, because they’re young men. Young Black men, and they were at school, and they didn’t understand why what was happening, happened to them.”.

Kamdang told NYT that “for anyone with children, that is a scary, scary situation. For a Black student, especially a young Black man in America, that is a life-or-death situation.”.

As AI tools are increasingly positioned as public safety solutions, the Lawyers Committee is pushing for police reform when cops or officials appear to be blindly trusting AI, their press release mentioned. They noted that “this injustice also raises a broader concern regarding the use and reliability of AI-powered technology in public safety where accuracy is essential in life-and-death situations.”.

Germany head into the knockout phase on a high note, not only because they won their group, but also the way they performed in their last two matches, against Serbia and the Netherlands in the group stage.

Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp followed the draw, held in Nyon on Friday, from the German FA's (DFB) Frankfurt offices. He played down the notion that Germany enter the tie as the favorites.

Industry observers note that "I've practically never given it any thought. It's never interested me," he noted.

According to recent reports, "An awful lot can happen in that time. We're very happy with the final impression we left, yet we're also fully aware that we're only at the very beginning of a development process. We want to carry this positive momentum forward—there's still a great deal to be done.".

The matches are slated for March 25 and March 30, 2027, and having won their group, Germany will have home-field advantage for the second leg.

Germany and Belgium have faced each other 26 times to date, with West Germany and Germany having the upper hand with 20 wins, five defeats and one draw.

Should Germany advance to the semifinals, they will go on to face the winner of England and Norway – a World Cup quarterfinals rematch.

In the other two semifinals matchups, the Netherlands drew Portugal, while the top pairing sees Spain face France in a rematch of one of last summer's World Cup semifinals.

The "Final Four" mini tournament is to be held from June 9 to 13 but the host venue won't be determined until the semifinal lineup has been completed.

Hims & Hers introduces new peptide treatments — while admitting there's more to learn about efficacy

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1581 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that hims & Hers Health on Wednesday said it will offer five formulations of peptides and longevity treatments compounded in the U.S.
  • Even as it confirmed the upcoming products, Hims & Hers acknowledged it has more to learn about how best to use the peptides and how effective they are — underscoring the uncertainty surrounding the growing space.
  • It has been revealed that the upcoming offerings come after the federal government eased restrictions on compounding certain unapproved peptides, which are short chains of amino ​acids.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that hims & Hers Health on Wednesday said it will offer five formulations of peptides and longevity treatments compounded in the U.S. as part of the initial rollout of its Peptides+ platform, all of which are not approved by regulators.

Even as it confirmed the upcoming products, Hims & Hers acknowledged it has more to learn about how best to use the peptides and how effective they are — underscoring the uncertainty surrounding the growing space.

It has been revealed that the upcoming offerings come after the federal government eased restrictions on compounding certain unapproved peptides, which are short chains of amino ​acids. Those products have exploded in popularity among fitness and longevity enthusiasts who attest that they help with muscle growth, rapid injury recovery and anti-aging, even though most lack evidence from robust human trials.

Hims in late October debuted an early access list for the upcoming peptide offerings, and more than 10,000 people signed up within 15 days, a company spokesperson noted in a statement.

It has been revealed that none of the company's specific compounded products are approved by the Food and Drug Administration. But Hims remarked they are authorized by law and formulated by pharmacies "that adhere to rigorous quality standards and are licensed and inspected by state boards of pharmacy.".

The products include compounded formulations of sermorelin, a peptide that stimulates growth-hormone release and is marketed for recovery, body composition and anti-aging; glutathione, a peptide promoted ‌for anti-aging and athletic recovery; and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, or NAD+, a coenzyme that plays a role in cellular metabolism.

According to recent reports, the company will also offer compounded versions of vitamin B-12, a vitamin needed to make red blood cells, build DNA, and maintain healthy nerve function, and L-carnitine, an amino acid derivative that helps the body turn fat into energy. The FDA has approved certain prescription forms of both peptides for established medical uses, primarily for diagnosed deficiencies in those compounds.

Hims mentioned it intends to add more peptides and therapies made in the U.S. over time. That includes BPC-157, an unapproved peptide derived from a protein found in human gastric juice that is marketed for healing processes. The company also aims to introduce another unapproved peptide called TB-500, which is derived from a naturally occurring protein in the body and is marketed for broader, systemic soft-tissue recovery and flexibility. Most of the research on both has been conducted in animals, not humans.

To receive the products, members on the Hims platform will start with an assessment of health history and goals with a licensed provider trained in peptide therapies, who can tailor a personalized plan to their needs, if appropriate.

The company said it intends to use its communication platform to check in with patients and ensure they are seeing desired results.

Sources indicate that "If they're not, we need to do something about it," Dr. Anant Vinjamoori, Hims chief medical officer, told CNBC. "We need to, you know, adjust the dose when that's appropriate, or in some cases consider other compounds that's maybe a better fit. And of course, there will also be cases when we need to refer people to other care options.".

However, Vinjamoori noted there's still uncertainty over how to best use the peptides.

"We don't have all of this data that we're used to having with compounds like this," he noted. "We have the opportunity to get it right, and I think we see that as our responsibility with a firm of our size, our skill, and resources to really lead.".

Vinjamoori added that people who have serious illnesses, such as cardiovascular disease, liver disease and kidney disease, will not be candidates for the compounds for now.

Meanwhile, Andrew Huberman, a well known neuroscientist, podcaster and Stanford University School of Medicine professor who recently joined Hims' board of directors, in a statement called compounds "real medical treatments, not just a wellness trend." He noted Hims provides safe access through "trusted sourcing and physician oversight.".

It has been revealed that but health experts raised concerns about the broader mainstream marketing of peptides in the U.S. and accessing them on telehealth platforms.

Industry observers note that "With peptides, I think you have to view them the same way you would view any drug that hasn't been rigorously tested," said Joshua Kritzer, a chemistry professor at Tufts University. "Without actual testing, all you have is anecdotal information, and that's just not enough information to put a substance in your body.".

Kritzer stated the lack of large clinical trials means researchers can't rule out potentially serious, rare complications from peptides — the kinds of risks that have led regulators to reject or pull otherwise effective drugs from the market after they underwent comprehensive testing in humans.

Without that testing, it's also unclear how telehealth firms, physicians and pharmacies can make decisions about what doses patients should take, said Paul Knoepfler, a cell biology and human anatomy professor at UC Davis Health. While some people rely on anecdotal data from real peptide consumers, "the dosing for these products really has not been established," he added.

Knoepfler remarked one risk is that injecting too much of a synthetic peptide into patients could trigger "weird immune responses that are really bad for one's health" because the body might recognize it as foreign.

"With the peptides, it's very loosey-goosey," Knoepfler told CNBC. "How does one even know what would be the effective amount for whatever you're hoping it will do, and what amount would have more risks?".

It has been revealed that but he stated the more contact patients can have with physicians around taking a compounded peptide, the better. Providers, including those tied to telehealth firms, should make sure patients are well-informed about the possible risks and unknowns of a given product and consider their preexisting conditions, cancer history and other medications, Knoepfler said.

That appears to be consistent with the approach Hims & Hers is taking. The manufacturer says patients who use the peptide and longevity products can also use its Care+ offering, which pairs treatment with ongoing support. That includes twice-a-year lab testing to track their progress and the ability to message providers trained in peptide therapy around the clock with any questions.

Still, Kritzer argued that having a doctor who only knows a patient from online, essentially mail-order platforms or websites "is not enough supervision to put you on a prescription medication," especially an unapproved one.

In a recent development, hims' ability to legally sell some of these peptides stems from a major shift in federal oversight by the Health and Human Services Department. It issued a policy in October that says the Food and Drug Administration will not take enforcement action against licensed pharmacies, federal facilities or physicians that compound and dispense six unapproved peptides while formal rules are reviewed.

In a recent development, in practice, that means these pharmacies and other firms can now offer them, even though the peptides aren't yet on the FDA's official list of ingredients compounding pharmacies are allowed to make. It does not translate to formal approval of the specific peptides.

The policy followed a 2023 decision by the Biden administration where the FDA restricted compounding pharmacies from producing popular peptide formulations due to safety, impurity and immune-reaction concerns.

HHS Secretary ​Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has supported broader access to peptides, calling himself a "major fan" of the treatments and arguing that restrictions were driving Americans to potentially unsafe products from overseas. Kennedy has previously described using BPC-157 to treat a muscle injury.

The announcement also comes after Hims in February 2025 acquired a California-based peptide manufacturing facility equipped with advanced peptide synthesizers.

The evidence for peptide efficacy varies by compound.

A 2026 systematic review screening 113 studies, including both small trials on humans along with rodent research, found zero eligible clinical outcome trials proving that administering IV or intramuscular NAD+ improves anti-aging, energy, or wellness endpoints in humans.

It has been revealed that there is some evidence for specific uses of certain peptides, such as potential weight loss. A review of 37 L-carnitine trials found participants lost about 2.7 pounds on average, though that analysis does not demonstrate that a compounded injection works the same way.

Meanwhile, vitamin B-12 injections are most commonly used to help people with a diagnosed deficiency rather than preventative care. U.S. survey data reveals only 3.6% of adults are B-12 deficient.

In a recent development, glutathione's evidence is thin, too. IV injections of it are widely marketed for skin whitening, yet not FDA-approved for this purpose.

A small study published in the Journal of Pakistan Association of Dermatologists evaluating IV glutathione indicated that the treatment is "not very effective" for skin-lightening, and that it loses efficacy with time.

The FDA also stated in August that it received reports of at least 30 patients who experienced adverse events after they received compounded IV glutathione alone or in combination with other ingredients from different compounding pharmacies.

In a recent development, all of the glutathione tied to the reports were from the same wholesale distributor and was labeled as dietary supplement grade, which is not an appropriate ingredient to make injectable drugs. Two of the Texas pharmacies conducted recalls related to elevated endotoxin levels in their glutathione injectable drugs.

These studies and reports don't speak to how Hims' exact combination will perform, but they do highlight the current limits on data studying the treatments and the questions surrounding them.

Breaking: Trump turns White House press conference into a 2028 succession audition

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1371 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The president appeared to put Vance and Rubio through their paces as potential successors, though Stephen Miller unexpectedly stole the spotlight.
  • The ageing King Lear’s question to his daughters, expecting them to compete for his favour and carve up his kingdom, hovered in the White House press briefing room on Friday.
  • There at the lectern stood Donald “Lear” Trump.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The president appeared to put Vance and Rubio through their paces as potential successors, though Stephen Miller unexpectedly stole the spotlight.

“Which of you shall we say doth love us most?”.

The ageing King Lear’s question to his daughters, expecting them to compete for his favour and carve up his kingdom, hovered in the White House press briefing room on Friday.

There at the lectern stood Donald “Lear” Trump. Behind him stood his potential heirs, JD “Goneril” Vance and Marco “Regan” Rubio, and to the side sat Trump’s favourite offspring, Stephen “Cordelia” Miller (more of him later). As for Lear’s Fool, the choices were endless.

According to recent reports, ostensibly this was a press conference to trumpet the president’s trip in Asia, but in practice everyone knew it was the first audition for the 2028 presidential election (and boy, is Trump going to enjoy turning the race into a contest for his approval). Vance is widely expected to seek the crown, though it was Rubio who came out on top in the latest Emerson College national poll.

In a jam-packed room, Trump stood centre stage as if hosting The Apprentice all over again. Behind him were the two contenders expressing their aspirations through matching suits, matching Maga red ties, matching US flag pins and matching leather shoes.

It has been revealed that the first trial: could Vance and Rubio stand still for 90 minutes without rolling their eyes, yawning or silently mouthing “Kill me!” to the press? Could they force Trump’s word salad down their throats and look as if they were enjoying it? Even when the boss was rambling at length about potholes?

“When you fix a pothole”, began one detour by the octogenarian president. “I don’t want to bore you – they’ll say, oh, he rambled, he rambled terribly. I don’t ramble. I don’t ramble at all, but when you fix a pothole, you have brand new asphalt against old white asphalt that doesn’t look good, but at least you don’t ruin your car, but these roads were flawless …”.

But first, the whole thing got off to a strange start. Trump appeared at the podium and remarked: “That’s a massive, big a crowd. I’ve never seen this before,” but reporters crammed in the room could barely hear him above the whoosh of an air conditioning unit. An engineer tweaked the sound, but it only gave Trump’s voice an eerie echo.

It has been revealed that had the gremlins that grounded flights and frozen banking sites finally reached the White House? So much for America the hi-tech superpower. Eventually order was restored, though not necessarily in Trump’s brain.

Recent findings suggest that he was evidently flattered by the media comparing his trilateral summit with the leaders of China and Russia to the Yalta meeting between Winston Churchill, Franklin Roosevelt and Joseph Stalin (he did not say which of the three he identified with, though critics could take a guess). Like a gushing teenager, Trump was so thrilled that Chinese president Xi Jinping had come to the airport to greet him, that he mentioned it twice (“He didn’t meet Sleepy Joe with the plane, that I can tell you.”).

According to recent reports, the US, Russia and China hold 92% of global nuclear power, he noted, which gave him an excuse to bring up his uncle John Trump, an electrical engineer and former Massachusetts Institute of Technology professor. “A member of my family spent his life at MIT who they say is now the greatest professor in the history of MIT, so I have great understanding of- I guess maybe genetically I’m blessed,” Trump riffed.

It has been revealed that at that remark Rubio could resist no longer. A smile spread across his lips and he shot a look at Vance, who felt obliged to smile back. We’re not laughing at you, we’re laughing with you, Mr President.

Indeed, Rubio had been the more fidgety of the pair. As Trump chuntered on, the secretary of state had shifted from foot to foot, fiddled with his tie, played with his lower lip, touched up his hair and given the odd wry smile. Vance, meanwhile, hid behind his beard and miasma of smugness.

But then, at last, came the moment for Lear’s daughters to make their public declarations of love. Vance went up the lectern and pointed out that he had stayed in Washington rather than joining the trip, comparing himself to Macaulay Culkin’s character in Home Alone – a child who is accidentally left behind at Christmas as his family rushes to catch a flight to Paris. “I missed you, sir,” he said to Trump, before praising the president for “securing historic trade deals” and reorganising the global economy to benefit the American worker and economy.

Industry observers note that not bad, but a little wonky. Marco, you’re up next. The secretary of state took aim at the critics who accused Trump of cosying up to dictators at the expense of Democrats, raising his eyebrows and shaking his fist: “These three countries possess the overwhelming majority of nuclear weapons on this planet. The idea that these three leaders should not engage on a regular basis is not just absurd, it’s dangerous.”.

Trump began taking reporters’ questions. One young whippersnapper posed a question that will be asked many times over the next two years. “Because you have the vice-president, the secretary of state right behind you, I’m curious which of them do you think would make a better president after you?”.

According to recent reports, trump swatted it aside without answering. Vance remained stony faced. Rubio smiled knowingly.

The same reporter put Vance in an uncomfortable spot by asking about his post-midterm tweet. “Would you argue that the war in Iran was worth it to lose the Senate?” The vice-president agreed with the goal of Iran not getting a nuclear weapon but added carefully: “I think the president is the one who makes the decision and the president has said he would do it again. And my view is that my goal is and my job is to support the president of the United States.”.

It has been revealed that in other words, I hate this war and would never have started it but I have to back the boss. Expect a lot more of this needle-threading in the upcoming campaign.

Recent findings suggest that later, when Trump asked “Do you want to keep this going or not” amid a cacophony of shouted questions, he turned around to look at Rubio, who laughed, then at Vance, who did likewise with folded arms. The two rivals patted each other playfully. But neither was prepared for the man who would steal their thunder.

“We have the most powerful man in the world in the room right now,” said Trump, referring to Miller, the recently appointed White House chief of ideological zealotry, who stepped up to the lectern with bald pate gleaming under the bright lights.

“I just wanted to say that what President Trump has achieved over the last two years is more than any president has achieved by far in American history!” Miller roared, before offering the kind of vainglorious soliloquy that would make even a Kremlin or Chinese Communist party spokesperson blush. “What you’re going to see over the next two years, as astonishing as that has been under his leadership, the next two years are going to be the greatest two years in American history!”.

Industry observers note that trump, who loves nothing more than flattery with exclamation marks, returned to the lectern and unveiled: “We have breaking news. We have breaking news.” Waving his hands, then with thumbs pointed at Vance and Rubio, he noted of Miller: “He was better than these two guys. Do you want to run for president?”.

Recent findings suggest that that was a joke, right? Trump was stirring the succession pot again, making his potential heirs uncomfortable. It was fitting that he ended the press conference reminiscing about the night he hosted Ultimate Fighting Championship bouts on the White House South Lawn. He is going to relish every moment of presiding over a Republican cage match for the next two years.

Is Pakistan backing anti-Taliban groups in Afghanistan?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (934 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Taliban authorities in Afghanistan claim that the Pakistani government is supporting armed Afghan groups that are opposed to their rule, an accusation Islamabaddenies.
  • Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi recently alleged that Pakistan had released a "project to destabilize Afghanistan.".
  • He claimed that "thousands of armed individuals have gathered along the Durand Line [Afghanistan-Pakistan border] to undermine the stability achieved in Afghanistan.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Taliban authorities in Afghanistan claim that the Pakistani government is supporting armed Afghan groups that are opposed to their rule, an accusation Islamabaddenies.

Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi recently alleged that Pakistan had released a "project to destabilize Afghanistan.".

He claimed that "thousands of armed individuals have gathered along the Durand Line [Afghanistan-Pakistan border] to undermine the stability achieved in Afghanistan.".

The accusations come after months of border clashes between Afghan Taliban and Pakistani forces.

In July, the Afghanistan Freedom Front (AFF), an anti-Taliban group, reportedly clashed with Taliban forces in the Zebak district of Badakhshan, a northeastern Afghan province. The group said it also carried out attacks in Nooristan and Kunar provinces in October.

Another "resistance group," the United Front of Afghanistan, claimed it attacked Taliban forces in Kandahar province along the border with Pakistan.

"The people who created insecurity in Badakhshan crossed from Chitral [in Pakistan] and later fled back to Chitral. They had been brought in. Even Pakistani military personnel were with them," alleged Zabihullah Mujahid, the Taliban's main spokesperson, in an interview with DW's Pashto-Dari service in September.

Pakistan's Ministry of Information swiftly dismissed the allegations as propaganda.

Groups that oppose Taliban rule in Afghanistan say they are not supported by any external force, and their resistance is purely indigenous.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

More than five years since returning to power in Kabul, the Taliban have consolidated their control over Afghanistan and largely suppressed both armed resistance groups and political dissidents.

Shinkai Karokhail, a former Afghan lawmaker, told DW it would be logistically difficult for anti-Taliban Afghan groups to cross the Pakistani border and enter Afghanistan without Islamabad's support, referring to clashes in Badakhshan and Nooristan provinces. "It is simply impossible," she mentioned.

Industry observers note that the Taliban themselves maintained close ties with Pakistan in the 1990s during their first stint in power. Some US officials have even claimed that Islamabad didn't relinquish its support to the Islamist group even after the 2001 September 11 terrorist attacks in the United States. Islamabad has always refuted these allegations.

Afrasiab Khattak, a Pakistani political analyst and former senator, believes that Pakistani support for anti-Taliban groups is "real.".

"Taliban opponents come to Islamabad, hold meetings, and it is a part of Pakistan's policy toward Afghanistan," he told DW.

Qandil Abbas, an associate professor of politics and international relations at Quaid-i-Azam University in Islamabad, disagrees.

"Pakistan may provide political support [to Taliban opponents], but not military support," she told DW.

Ali Ahmad Jalali, a professor at the Near East South Asia Center for Strategic Studies at the National Defense University in Washington DC, said it is possible that Islamabad is backing opponents of the Taliban as "leverage.".

"When such incidents take place along the Afghanistan-Pakistan border, and given Pakistan's history of support for Afghan groups, it would not be surprising if Pakistan is supporting these groups," Jalali noted.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Pakistani officials have repeatedly demanded that the Taliban take action against anti-Pakistan militant groups, particularly the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), a militant group responsible for attacking Pakistani civilians and soldiers, and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), an outlawed armed separatist group active in its western Balochistan province.

Islamabad alleges that these groups organize and launch attacks on Pakistan from Afghan territory with Taliban support.

"Meaningful progress requires Afghan authorities to address legitimate security concerns of neighboring countries, particularly the threat of terrorism," Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said this week at the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) summit in Islamabad.

The Pakistani government stated on Friday that Afghanistan was not invited to participate in the ECO gathering as Pakistan does not recognize the Taliban regime in Kabul.

Jalali, who served as Afghanistan's interior minister from 2003 to 2005, argued that Islamabad is demanding something the Taliban may neither be willing nor able to provide.

It has been revealed that "Pakistan wants the Taliban to cooperate in fighting against groups such as the TTP. But the TTP has long fought alongside the Afghan Taliban. There are ideological as well as friendly ties between the two. They seek a similar political system, and some Afghan Taliban members may even be among TTP fighters," the analyst added.

Experts also point to the Taliban's efforts to strengthen relations with India, Pakistan's long-standing regional rival, as a cause of concern for Islamabad.

Malek Sitez, an Afghan international relations researcher, argued that Pakistan was not keen on Kabul getting closer to New Delhi but added that Pakistan no longer had the kind of influence over Afghanistan that it had in the past.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Despite accusations and counteraccusations from both sides, Jalali did not believe that Pakistan was seeking regime change in Afghanistan.

"I do not think Pakistan can or wants to overthrow the Taliban and replace them with another group," he underlined. Instead, he stressed, Islamabad's objective is to pressure the Taliban into cooperating against the TTP.

Aziz Barez, a political analyst, was of the view that Afghan groups opposed to the Taliban could not fully trust Islamabad, adding that they may welcome alleged Pakistani support but are also aware that such backing could be temporary.

"It is possible that Pakistan and the Taliban will resolve their differences tomorrow and become close allies again," he told DW.

Ahmad Waheed Ahmady and Helay Asad contributed to this report.

Man accused of sparking deadly Los Angeles wildfire found guilty

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (680 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Verdict in case against former Uber driver Jonathan Rinderknecht comes after first trial ended with hung jury.
  • The 30-year-old accused of sparking the deadly Palisades fire in Los Angeles was found guilty of two federal arson charges in a Friday verdict that came months after his first trial concluded with a hung jury.
  • For two weeks, a fresh batch of jurors listened to prosecutors mount their case against Jonathan Rinderknecht.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Verdict in case against former Uber driver Jonathan Rinderknecht comes after first trial ended with hung jury.

The 30-year-old accused of sparking the deadly Palisades fire in Los Angeles was found guilty of two federal arson charges in a Friday verdict that came months after his first trial concluded with a hung jury.

For two weeks, a fresh batch of jurors listened to prosecutors mount their case against Jonathan Rinderknecht.

They argued the former Uber driver was responsible for the January 2025 wildfire, which claimed 12 lives and devastated the Pacific Palisades, an affluent enclave on the California coast.

Recent findings suggest that rinderknecht, in prosecutors’ account, used a lighter to set a brush fire in the hillside area. The state cast him as a disgruntled young man who sought retribution against the world for personal gripes, including failed romances, and perceived societal injustices like wealth inequality.

Firefighters suppressed the so-called Lachman brush fire last January, but its embers simmered underground, before being swept by powerful winds and erupting above ground into the Palisades inferno that destroyed thousands of homes and businesses.

Rinderknecht had maintained his innocence, pleading not guilty to the revised charges of destruction of property by means of fire and arson affecting property used in interstate commerce.

For the retrial, jurors were instructed explicitly to not consider the adequacy of the fire department’s response to the Lachman and Palisades blaze. The department has faced criticism for failing to fully extinguish the Lachman fire that eventually reignited.

The note came after some of the first trial’s jurors were wary of pinning the blame squarely on Rinderknecht, citing the fire department’s past actions. Of that deadlocked panel, two voted for guilty, while 10 others were not convinced.

Rinderknecht’s defense team doubled down during the retrial on an alternative explanation for the Palisades fire, suggesting the initial brush blaze was ignited by fireworks.

Prosecutors dismissed the theory as “baseless” in a court filing where they raised concern over the reliability and late introduction of a defense witness, whose testimony would reference stains at a private residence that supposedly indicated fireworks had been discharged.

The state also presented digital evidence that cast doubt over Rinderknecht’s claim that he was at the bottom of a hiking trail when he saw the Lachman fire begin.

Industry observers note that “These lies are telling – they are not mistakes,” prosecutor Danbee Kim reportedly remarked at trial. “Because he knows that where he was when the fire started was incriminating.”.

Friday’s conviction followed two days of jury deliberation.

Standing outside a downtown Los Angeles courthouse on Friday, one juror cited the inconsistencies in Rinderknecht’s whereabouts during the fire as proof of his guilt.

“Logically, things started pointing towards him,” remarked Cameron, a 30-year-old college student who declined to give his last name to reporters.

Cameron stopped short of answering whether or not he believed Rinderknecht intended to burn down the Palisades.

He stated he believed Rinderknecht’s “intent was to start a fire” and that his actions resulted in the devastating blaze.

The city and county of Los Angeles continue to face civil lawsuits from survivors of the fire and victims’ families.

Friday’s guilty verdict may not bear much weight on that litigation.

“For the purpose of our civil case, the fire could have been started by lightning and would have had the same result,” stated Alex Robertson, an attorney representing fire victims in a consolidated suit.

“It doesn’t matter what started the fire. It’s what happened – what didn’t happen in terms of protecting the residents of the Palisades and Malibu after the fire started.”.

In a Friday statement, the outgoing Los Angeles mayor Karen Bass stated: “No verdict can bring back the lives lost or erase the pain families have endured.”.

In a recent development, “So many are still struggling to rebuild,” she continued. “For those still displaced, the devastation remains a daily reality.”.

Recent findings suggest that rinderknecht, who remains in federal custody, will be sentenced on 17 March. He is facing between five and 40 years in prison.

Breaking: Don Bluth on the future of animation and AI: Thats definitely a road I dont want to travel on

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For children of the '80s and '90s, Don Bluth was a major influence on how we saw the world.
  • Sources indicate that social media is evergreen with fans remembering the tender moments of Littlefoot and his tree star, or the terrifying ones, like Fievel or Mrs.
  • In a recent development, in an interview with Mashable, Bluth said watching the finished doc "brought tears to [his] eyes," because it refreshed memories of his colleagues.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For children of the '80s and '90s, Don Bluth was a major influence on how we saw the world. With movies like The Secret of NIMH, An American Tail, The Land Before Time, All Dogs Go to Heaven, and Anastasia, this American animator offered us realms of adventure, with plucky heroes as well as villains so fantastically frightening that we carry the thrill of it all with us decades later.

Sources indicate that social media is evergreen with fans remembering the tender moments of Littlefoot and his tree star, or the terrifying ones, like Fievel or Mrs. Brisby being chased down by monstrous, roaring, ravenous cats. Now, for fans upcoming and old, filmmakers Dave LaMattina and Chad N. Walker offer Don Bluth: Somewhere Out There, a documentary that explores the life and work of the innovative animator through his own words.

In a recent development, in an interview with Mashable, Bluth said watching the finished doc "brought tears to [his] eyes," because it refreshed memories of his colleagues. Together, they pursued animation not for the money but for the art and a deep desire to create something meaningful for future generations. Yet, when asked about his legacy, Bluth is quick to look back on the path that led him to his work.

He began by speaking of Winsor McCay, the father of American animation. In a wistful storyteller tone, Bluth recounted how a little boy witnessed the "magic" of the 1914 short film Gertie the Dinosaur, in which a pencil-sketched brontosaurus comes to life. This little boy was so inspired that he'd grow up to make his own animated short featuring a mouse named Mickey.

That little boy, of course, was Walt Disney, who would go on to make 1937's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, the first animated feature film produced in the United States. That movie would go on to inspire a young Bluth, who'd direct his first animated feature in 1982 with The Secret of NIMH.

This path of inspiration to iconic art wasn't as direct a line as you might think.

It has been revealed that yes, Bluth scored a dream job, working at Disney Animation studio for 10 years on films like Sleeping Beauty, Robin Hood, and The Rescuers. But after Disney's death in 1966, Bluth and 17 other Disney animators feared the studio had lost their way, creatively.

He told Mashable he'd invite these artists to his home on weekends, where they'd draw together to develop innovative pitches for their corporate bosses. When they were shot down, Bluth — along with Gary Goldman and John Pomeroy — built their own company, Don Bluth Productions, to "see if we could do better than they were doing." For this, Bluth remembered, "We were called traitors.".

In a recent development, that's not how Bluth saw his team. "[These] wonderful people had the courage to leave their jobs and security and go out there and try and do something great," he stated, "not just to feed their egos, but something they felt helped them grow up. And they wanted to give back.".

Sources indicate that it was not an easy journey, as Don Bluth: Somewhere Out There details, revealing the highs and lows of Bluth's most beloved and worst-reviewed productions, as well as the wildly popular video game Dragon's Lair. In our interview, he spoke repeatedly about how the doc filled him with gratitude as he looked back for the filmmakers' interviews.

To Mashable, he reflected, "What happened after so many movies, All Dogs Go to Heaven, American Tail, working with Steven Spielberg on both of those pictures, and George Lucas [on The Land Before Time], [it] became really, really obvious to us that we were doing the right thing [by] writing the right stories, and trying to make something that would move people's lives for the better — not just to pat our own backs and say, 'Look what we did.' [We were making] something that would help maybe children grow up and have some degree of morality about them. So then, that was our goal in everything.".

In Somewhere Out There, the rise of computer animation — which Bluth refers to as "3D animation" — came as a devastating blow to the animator, who'd spent his life developing the skills of hand-drawn 2D animation. To this day, Bluth still advocates for the artistry of hand-drawn animation.

"The way I look at this is animation in the 2D form is people, armed with a pencil in their hands, have to be able to draw," he explained, "and they also have to be able to act. And they have to have feelings about story.".

According to recent reports, to Bluth, CGI movies aren't animation. "3D animation is puppetry," he mentioned, adding, "[With 3D animation,] you drop your pencil. You put your hands on a keyboard, and you make a wireframe puppet act.".

Industry observers note that bluth shared several of his complaints about the look of 3D animation, saying, "To me, it looks very plastic... The colors are muted, and they're trying to put shading in there, trying to look more like a live-action picture." He asked, "Why are we trying to get to a place which looks more real?" adding, "That isn't the purpose at all of 2D [animation]. The purpose is to take you to a magical world. 2D is trying to make audiences come to our own world.".

Noting the animation industry changed forever with the massive success of 1995's Toy Story, Bluth noted, "Toy Story [movies] were quite fun to watch, but they didn't make me feel anything very deep. And animation is intended to do that, particularly with Walt Disney pictures. Snow White, Bambi, [and] Pinocchio — those pictures did something to change the way you thought and help you grow up in a way that was really good. And they did it in such a beautiful way.".

Industry observers note that it was when Disney Studios, post-Walt, moved away from these tenets that Bluth and his colleagues set out on their own. He mentioned, "We left the Disney Studio because it was leaving out the morality statements and leaving out all the beautiful colors and everything.".

In terms of what recent animated films impressed Bluth, he stated, "I liked Klaus a lot," commending Sergio Pablos' inventive Christmas tale, which employs hand-drawn animation with a unique visual style.

Sources indicate that bluth also enjoyed Pete Docter's 2009 Pixar hit Up. "That was totally in 3D," he noted, "but it had a great story. For my taste, it went on too long. You know, the story was really about this couple promising each other they would go back to some place in their life, and she died. So, the man, true to the promise, tries to fulfill that [by taking their house on the journey]. So, I love that.".

Sources indicate that overall though, Bluth lamented, "Animation has become an advertisement for sugar cereal and whatever. There are more advertisements on animation than there are actually animated characters. The animated characters are just simply little puppets that jump up and down and tell one-line jokes. So, that's not good. Now, the last laugh is about to hit us like a tsunami; that is AI.".

Sources indicate that through the stories of Russian Jewish immigrant Fievel Mousekewitz, the widowed mother of four Mrs. Brisby, the orphaned brontosaurus Littlefoot, and rogue mutt Charlie B. Barkin, Bluth was striving to create stories that would inspire children to be good and creative, as Disney's movies had done for him. He doesn't see a future where AI can provide such mindful, moral guidance.

Recent findings suggest that "It seems like AI is able to do wonderful, wonderful things," Bluth mused, "except AI is a machine, and it has no soul. It will borrow or steal, if you will, from everything that it knows, and give you what you ask for. But where's the creativity?".

According to recent reports, "AI is a borrower," Bluth explained. "When you enter what you'd like to see, it searches all over and borrows it from other artists, puts it together. It shows you on screen. Now, you can then make corrections. It can do all that, but it is still a machine. It doesn't ask you, 'Well, what is right and wrong? What is evil and good? What do you want me to say?' The machine can't do that.".

He continued, "The only thing you can do is go back to human beings and say, 'Don't replace human beings with machines.' They're the ones who have a heart, who have a soul, and probably have a Creator. So, there's a bigger picture that's going on than just animation on a screen.".

It has been revealed that "AI has no soul," Bluth concluded. "It hasn't a clue how to write anything. Everything that you're going to see on your screen has been stolen from other artists.".

He allowed that some AI might be "stunningly beautiful," but "you'll find that it doesn't affect your heart the way you feel… They're not artists that are doing the AI. Many of them don't understand the art of acting or anything. So, what everything looks like in AI animation that I've seen, it all looks like slow motion, and it looks unreal. So, that's definitely a road I don't want to travel on.".

"I read somewhere where someone mentioned something that stuck in my head," he mused, paraphrasing Oscar Wilde's The Portrait of Dorian Gray. "There are many people who know the price of everything but the value of nothing. And I certainly hope that's not where we're going.".

Man hired by Russia spied on Silicon Valley tech and defense tech giant, feds say

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Russian national has been indicted on suspicions he was a Russian spy who stalked and surveilled employees of a Silicon Valley organization that was assisting Ukraine in its ongoing war with its eastern neighbor.
  • In a recent development, igor D’iu, 25, allegedly photographed the employees and their computer screens as they worked at a coffee shop located near the company’s Palo Alto office, federal prosecutors mentioned Wednesday.
  • It has been revealed that “FEMP1 made evasive and irregular turns, took back roads, and turned into a grocery store parking lot where D’IU continued aggressively following her vehicle,” an FBI special agent wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Russian national has been indicted on suspicions he was a Russian spy who stalked and surveilled employees of a Silicon Valley organization that was assisting Ukraine in its ongoing war with its eastern neighbor.

In a recent development, igor D’iu, 25, allegedly photographed the employees and their computer screens as they worked at a coffee shop located near the company’s Palo Alto office, federal prosecutors mentioned Wednesday. He also kept a list of home addresses of employees and a senior executive. At one point, prosecutors said, D’iu trailed an employee as she traveled home from Palo Alto to San Francisco. An affidavit filed in the case referred to the employee as FEMP1, short for female employee, and said the event left her “in a state of emotional distress.”.

It has been revealed that “FEMP1 made evasive and irregular turns, took back roads, and turned into a grocery store parking lot where D’IU continued aggressively following her vehicle,” an FBI special agent wrote. “D’IU followed FEMP1 through U-turns, illegal left turns, and ran a red light to stay with FEMP1 for nearly thirty miles. FEMP1 called 911 while driving and was instructed to drive directly to San Francisco Police Department (“SFPD”) Mission Station. Near SFPD Mission Station, FEMP1 flagged an SFPD patrol vehicle and reported the incident. D’IU left once FEMP1 made contact with the patrol vehicle.”.

When police later questioned D’iu about the incident, the defendant allegedly mentioned he saw a woman get into a car and thought she was “beautiful.” He then told the investigators that he followed her because he “wanted to ask her out on a date.”.

Industry observers note that prosecutors didn’t name the firm, but both Reuters and Bloomberg, citing unnamed people with knowledge of the case, identified it as Palantir. Ars is unable to confirm that reporting. Palantir representatives didn’t respond to an email seeking confirmation.

D’iu allegedly entered the US unlawfully in the summer of 2026 after being recruited by someone over Telegram. Prosecutors said the party gave D’iu a clandestine assignment to target employees of a large technology and defense tech giant. D’iu received instructions, equipment, and financial support along with information that his work was on behalf of “the motherland.” His instructions were to collect information about the company because it was supplying weapons for use against Russian forces in Ukraine.

According to recent reports, prosecutors mentioned D’iu traveled from Istanbul, Turkey, to Mexico City in June. He then crossed the border into the US and was instructed to buy laptops, cell phones, wireless networking equipment, and remote access software. Besides instructions to monitor company employees at the coffee shop, D’iu’s orders also included positioning his laptop at certain locations near the company so it could be remotely accessed in an attempt to collect information from company employees nearby.

Industry observers note that D’iu allegedly obtained fraudulent identification documents to conceal his identity as he conducted his activities. The documents included a falsified California ID card, an altered US passport, and a Social Security card bearing the assumed name of “Hugo Landry Johns.” The passport was allegedly an authentic US passport that originally had been issued to someone elsewhere in the country. It was modified to display D’iu’s photograph and assumed identity.

Industry observers note that D’iu was arrested on October 30 and remains in custody. He is charged with one count of Conspiracy to Act as an Agent of a Foreign Government, one count of Acting as an Agent of a Foreign Government Without Notice to the Attorney General, and one count of Interstate Stalking. If convicted for Acting as an Agent of a Foreign Government Without Notice to the Attorney General, he faces a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison, a fine of $250,000, and three years of supervised release. He faces a maximum sentence of five years in prison, a fine of $250,000, and three years of supervised release for each conviction on the other two charges.

D’iu had his initial appearance in federal court on November 2. He is next scheduled to appear in federal court on November 24.

Breaking: iOS 27.3 Apple Intelligence, Siri AI usage limits: What to know

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1290 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • All good things must come to an end implement usage limits.
  • According to recent reports, just a few months after Apple finally launched the long-awaited Siri AI, its upgraded voice assistant powered by Apple Intelligence, the company will now implement daily usage limits.
  • Basically, if a user hits those limits, they will need to upgrade their paid iCloud+ account or wait for the daily limits to reset.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

All good things must come to an end implement usage limits.

According to recent reports, just a few months after Apple finally launched the long-awaited Siri AI, its upgraded voice assistant powered by Apple Intelligence, the company will now implement daily usage limits. These latest restrictions will be implemented along with the launch of iOS 27.3.

What does this mean? Basically, if a user hits those limits, they will need to upgrade their paid iCloud+ account or wait for the daily limits to reset. However, not every Siri AI request counts towards consumers' daily limits.

So, what counts towards your daily Siri AI limits? How much does it cost to upgrade? Lets break down everything you need to know about the upcoming Siri AI usage limits.

According to Apple, "Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features are available for free for owners with a supported device set to a supported language." However, "some features rely on powerful server models and have limits.".

Apple says the following features will have daily usage limits:.

Images: Intelligent Photo Editing Tools, which include Clean Up, Extend, and Spatial Reframing, as well as Image Playground.

Workflows and automation: AFM Cloud and AFM Cloud Pro models in Shortcuts.

Third-party apps that use Apple Foundation Models in Private Cloud Compute.

According to recent reports, apple has not published exactly what the daily usage limits are for Apple Intelligence or Siri AI. The company's Support page simply describes it as a "generous daily usage limit.".

It has been revealed that notably, each of those above categories has its own unique daily usage limits. These are not shared between those features, which means a user can hit the daily limit for one but not the others.

Daily usage limits are connected at the Apple account level and are implemented across all Apple devices, including iOS devices, Mac, and Apple TV.

Sources indicate that when a user reaches their daily limit, they will receive a prompt after making a request that counts towards those limits. Advanced requests are paused until the daily limit resets or the user upgrades to an iCloud+ proposal.

"Daily Request Limit Reached," the prompt reads on iOS. "You can continue with basic requests.".

The prompt also includes a button to upgrade to an iCloud+ strategy to increase those daily limits.

As previously mentioned, Apple isn't sharing exactly what those Apple Intelligence and Siri AI limits are. However, they have shared just how many times those "generous" limits are increased when upgrading to an iCloud+ plan.

In a recent development, here's an outline of what you get with each iCloud+ plan: The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile Products available for purchase through affiliate links. If you buy something through links on our site, Mashable may earn an affiliate commission.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

200GB: $2.99 per month – Up to 2x daily usage limit.

2TB: $9.99 per month – Up to 5x daily usage limit.

6TB: $29.99 per month – Up to 10x daily usage limit.

12TB: $59.99 per month – Up to 20x daily usage limit.

The 50GB iCloud+ strategy, which Apple sells for $0.99 per month, does not include any increase in daily usage limits for Apple Intelligence and Siri AI.

Apple states that all feature categories will have their daily limits reset at approximately midnight in the user's current time zone.

According to Apple, users who are travelling internationally will have their limits reset "around midnight in the central time zone of the country or region of your Apple Account." Users who share an iCloud+ strategy with a Family Sharing group will see their limits reset at around midnight of the time zone of the iCloud+ plan purchaser. Users who aren't signed into their Apple Account will see their limits reset around 24 hours after they first used that feature category that day.

Unused limits from the previous day do not roll over.

Starting with iOS 27.3, Siri AI will also receive limits for certain "advanced" tasks. Apple says that basic tasks will continue to be unlimited and will work even when the daily usage limits for advanced tasks are reached.

You may be wondering what a "basic" task is and what is an "advanced" task, the latter of which will have daily usage limits.

Apple provided the following examples as a basic task, which consumers will be able to utilize without limits:.

"Set a timer for three minutes.".

"Text Mark that Annika's party is at 123 Main Street.”.

As for advanced tasks, Apple provides these examples:.

"Text Mark the address for Annika's party, and tell him what time we need to leave from home to make it on time.".

"Add a summary of my San Francisco trip note to this email draft.".

Based on those examples, it appears advanced tasks involve multi-step requests that require server-side processing.

Beyond Apple's official published examples, Apple leaker pdfu has uncovered Apple's more detailed instructions given to Siri AI telling the assistant how to decide if a user has reached their limits for advanced tasks. In an X post, the leaker explained Siri will take limits into account if a user request:.

uses information from one app, from what is on screen or from a message, in a different app, or needs a result from one step used in a different step or app (such as a looked-up fact typed into a field).

contains two or more separate asks in one sentence, even in the same app (extra details of one action, such as a cc or a time, are still one ask).

asks about or summarizes the content of a photo, a camera view or an attachment (editing, searching and albums are fine).

deletes, archives, junks, moves, marks or changes a set (all, every, these or a whole category) of the user’s emails, notes, reminders, messages, photos, files, contacts or events.

sets a device action or a notification to run on a time or trigger (not alarms, timers, reminders or calendar events), notifies someone when a person arrives or leaves, or builds or edits a Shortcut or automation.

is deep research or a multi-step task done on the user’s behalf.

asks you to compose or create latest content (a story, poem, essay, blueprint, recipe, image, or an email or message from a topic rather than wording the user gives), or to rewrite in a tone other than friendly, professional or concise.

A user asking a third-party AI assistant like ChatGPT for an advanced request is never limited, even if a user reaches their daily usage limit for the day.

According to pdfu, tasks like "proofreading, rewriting in a friendly, professional or concise tone, summaries as key points, a list or a table, typing or sending wording the user gives, a single direct operation in any app, even when Siri must look the target up first (the closest bakery, my cousin), 'this' or 'that' within its own app, running a Shortcut by name, a reminder for yourself by time or place, Find My, sharing your ETA or location, and all your home accessories (lights, doors, locks), alarms, timers or device settings" all fall under basic tasks.

So far, Apple hasn't released much more on these newly introduced daily usage limits for Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. Hopefully, before iOS 27.3 comes out, Apple provides users with more specific information regarding what does and doesn't count towards their daily usage limits.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The announcement from Rockstar Games would mean GTA VI has already earned more than the entire box office run of the highest-grossing film of all time.

Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79bn in retail sales on its first day, publisher Rockstar Games has revealed, calling it the biggest launch for any entertainment product in history.

Industry observers note that the worldwide figure was based on tech giant estimates through the end of the day Thursday, the day the game debuted. Rockstar said also it had sold 32.5m units of the game on prerelease, setting a record across platforms.

“We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you,” Sam Houser, Rockstar’s president and founder, noted in a statement.

The tech giant said the sales set “a latest record for entertainment across any medium … becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.”.

The figure is nearly five times the roughly $800m that predecessor Grand Theft Auto V attracted during its first 24 hours in 2013.

It also exceeds the entire box office run of Avengers: Endgame, which became the highest-grossing film of all time last month at about $2.9bn worldwide after a rerelease pushed it past Avatar.

The game went on sale Thursday on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, launching first in New Zealand and rolling out market by market as each reached midnight local time.

The release promptly became a global phenomenon, generating more social media posts than this year’s World Cup, according to monitoring platform Visibrain.

Critics praised the game, which has a score of 99 on review aggregator Metacritic.

Rockstar noted that made it the highest-rated game ever.

Like its predecessors, “GTA VI” is an open-world action game in which players roam freely through a sprawling city, stealing cars, pulling off heists and carrying out missions for criminal gangs.

Its busy streets, neon-lit nightlife and beaches are rendered in striking detail, and non-player characters go about their lives whether or not the player is involved.

While critics have raved about the game, it has also prompted real-world warnings from authorities.

With the game’s release on Thursday, police departments across the US reminded people that the car thefts, reckless driving, violence and other criminal mayhem depicted in the blockbuster title should not be re-enacted on the country’s streets.

It has been revealed that there is insufficient evidence supporting a scientific causal link between violent video games and violent behaviour, according to the American Psycyhological Association. Nonetheless, several police departments took to the internet with warnings – and even jokes – aimed at keeping GTA VI’s lawlessness firmly in the virtual world.

The Atlanta police department delivered one of the clearest messages in a social media post.

Recent findings suggest that “GTA is not a real place, but Atlanta is!” the department warned. “Don’t confuse virtual entertainment with real-life decisions.”.

With the Associated Press and Agence France-Presse.

Internet Archive Staffers Are Unionizing

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (623 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Staffers at the Internet Archive, the nonprofit “digital library” that runs the Wayback Machine, are voting to join the Communications Workers of America (CWA).
  • Industry observers note that more than 80 of the 124 eligible US staffers voted in favor of unionizing, and they are currently awaiting voluntary recognition of the union from Internet Archive founder Brewster Kahle.
  • The Internet Archive, which also offers free catalogs preserving tens of millions of digital and physical media items, was founded by Kahle in 1996.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Staffers at the Internet Archive, the nonprofit “digital library” that runs the Wayback Machine, are voting to join the Communications Workers of America (CWA).

Industry observers note that more than 80 of the 124 eligible US staffers voted in favor of unionizing, and they are currently awaiting voluntary recognition of the union from Internet Archive founder Brewster Kahle. Kahle did not immediately respond to WIRED’s request for comment. If Kahle does not grant voluntary recognition, employees will vote whether to certify the union in a process run by the National Labor Relations Board.

The Internet Archive, which also offers free catalogs preserving tens of millions of digital and physical media items, was founded by Kahle in 1996. Kahle’s mission was to provide “Universal Access to All Knowledge.” Will Howes, an Internet Archive engineer, indicates that the organizing process has demonstrated how “aligned” employees are in their passion for Kahle’s goals.

“Frankly, we really see the formation of this union as accepting [Kahle’s] challenge to make this workplace the best place it can be in pursuit of a mission, universal access to all knowledge,” Howes tells WIRED.

Industry observers note that microfiche digitization technician Danielle Leard tells WIRED that the union is “very optimistic” that Kahle will voluntarily recognize it and come to the bargaining table. They add that among the union’s core goals are securing wage increases and additional benefits, and ensuring that these benefits are consistently available to employees across the tech giant.

“We believe the first and most primary goal of our union is to make sure that the Internet Archive reflects the wants and values of the people that work there, and the people that make the archive,” Leard notes.

Howes and Leard tell WIRED that the Internet Archive—which claims to have archived more than 1 trillion web pages—employs a highly diverse set of workers, including librarians, engineers, physical media specialists, and facility coordinators who maintain the archive’s building, a former Christian Scientist church in San Francisco. Leard says that the staff’s diversity has made the organizing process, which began in February 2025, “a unique challenge,” but one that’s “really rewarding.”.

In a recent development, the vote comes slightly more than two months after staffers at the Wikimedia Foundation, the nonprofit behind Wikipedia, voted to join CWA. Howes says the simultaneous efforts are “very powerful” given that both organizations represent “core infrastructure” of the internet.

Howes claims that the union wants to ensure that the 30-year-old project continues to thrive in the long term—and that its workers do too. Leard says this means providing paths for developing skills and getting promoted within the nonprofit.

Leard indicates that the Internet Archive’s unionization drive is especially important in the present moment, amid waves of tech layoffs and widespread anxiety about “emerging technologies” like AI.

The Internet Archive hasn’t been immune from the consequences of AI. A Nieman Lab report from January found that some news websites, struggling to prevent companies like OpenAI or Anthropic from harvesting their articles, have started blocking web crawlers from the Internet Archive, arguing it gives AI companies a back door to their content. (The archive relies on web crawlers to preserve news articles in near-real time.).

Leard says that ideally, the Internet Archive’s unionization will be “one domino” in a larger process that makes the tech industry better.

“We're hoping,” they say, “that we'll continue to be one of the blueprints that will make it easier for other organizations and companies in the future to continue to unionize.”.

Revision: 11/20/26 1:43pm ET: This story has been updated to reflect that Internet Archive workers have voted in favor of unionizing, but the union has not yet been recognized by Internet Archive founder Brewster Kahle.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The pair had taken off from the Scottish Gliding Centre at nearby Portmoak on a training flight.

Two men have been killed after their glider crashed into Loch Leven, a large body of water in Perth and Kinross, on Friday morning.

Police Scotland mentioned their bodies were recovered from the loch by the emergency services after the alarm was raised at 11.05am on Friday.

The force said next of kin had been told and the incident was not being treated as suspicious. Two HM Coastguard helicopters and an air ambulance were sent to the scene, along with a fire service appliance and a specialist crew.

The pair had taken off from the Scottish Gliding Centre at Portmoak airfield near the loch’s eastern shore in a Perkoz two-person glider on a training flight.

A spokesperson for the gliding centre stated: “The incident is at the moment under investigation by the Air Accident Investigation Branch [AAIB] of the Department for Transport and the police in conjunction with the British Gliding Association.

It has been revealed that “Our club is cooperating fully with these organisations. At the present time, there is no indication as to the cause of the accident.”.

An AAIB spokesperson mentioned: “A multidisciplinary team including inspectors with expertise in aircraft operations, engineering and recorded data have been deployed to gather evidence and make inquiries.”.

The police remarked airspace restrictions had been put in place after the crash was reported.
